Skywork AI · 2026 · 5B

Causal DiT with 3D re-projected patch memory

Causal DiTread

Details
Overview

Matrix-Game 3.5 returns to a fully causal generator and moves memory out of the KV cache into geometry: historical VAE-latent patches are lifted to 3D with metric depth, re-projected into the target view and inserted as tokens, so each 3-latent-frame chunk attends to a bounded pose-aware sequence of noisy targets, one clean anchor, a few context frames, patch-memory tokens and a reference prefix. Camera pose enters through tiled PRoPE with no new parameters. A 3-step causal student reaches 20 fps at 1280x704 on one H100 with INT8, GPU retrieval and a 75%-pruned decoder (company claim).

Representation

Wan2.2 VAE 4x16x16 + patchify (2x2 assumed) → 880 tokens per 22x40 latent frame at 1280x704, 2,640 per 3-latent chunk of 12 frames [D]; 48 latent channels

Core

Wan2.2-TI2V-5B DiT: 30 layers, d 3072, 24 heads, FFN 14336 (HF config); the full DiT is fine-tuned with the text encoder and VAE frozen; the only learnable additions are the reference-token embeddings

Attention

Block-causal chunks of 3 latent frames over one pose-aware sequence: noisy targets + clean anchor + context frames (1 per chunk in causal training, up to 5 in base training) + patch-memory tokens (≤1 per target cell) + a reference prefix of ≈1 frame; ≤≈7,900 tokens per chunk [D], bounded by ≈2.3x the target track; training window 1 anchor + 7 chunks = 22 latent positions

Actions

Camera pose via tiled PRoPE in every block: after RoPE, queries × Pᵀ, keys and values × P⁻¹, outputs × P, tiled over all head channels, no new parameters; translations recentred on the first target frame and log-compressed

Prediction

Perceptual flow matching causal adaptation (10k steps), then curriculum self-rollout DMD (1,000 outer steps, 5:1 update ratio) → 3-step causal generator; prefix and chunk-local context held at the next noise level each substep (HiAR), anchor clean

Decoder

MG-LightVAE, 75%-pruned Wan2.2 decoder → 12 frames per chunk at 1280x704; 'VAE decoding becomes the primary latency bottleneck' once the DiT is accelerated

Memory

Patch memory (MosaicMem-style): patches lifted to 3D with metric depth and poses, frustum-queried, z-buffered and scattered into a target-aligned memory frame; retrieval and dynamic-object filtering run once per segment, off the per-frame loop; the sequence does not grow with rollout length

Speed

Up to 20 output frames/s at 1280x704, batch 1, one H100, including the INT8 3-step DiT, online retrieval and MG-LightVAE decode (company claim; the VLM prompt rewriter runs asynchronously); 10.9 one-minute videos/hour at 77.0 GB peak on one H100 in the SANA-WM benchmark, undistilled model (authors' Table 1)

Key detail

Memory is geometry, not cache: the per-chunk sequence is capped at ≈2.3x the target track, so DiT cost is constant in rollout length and the depth, lift and projection work sits off the per-frame critical path

Status and sources

arXiv preprint (company). Availability: code + weights. Sources: arXiv 2608.29910 Sec. 2.1 (tiled PRoPE), 2.2 (patch, context and reference memory), 2.3 (distillation), 4.1 (implementation), 4.4 (real-time inference), Table 1; HF Wan-AI/Wan2.2-TI2V-5B config.json (local copy: 30 layers, dim 3072, 24 heads, ffn 14336, 48 latent channels); Wan2.2 README (VAE compression 4x16x16; local copy); code link on the paper's title page (weights release not verified in this pass).

NVIDIA · 2026 · 16B Nano

Reasoner and generator towers share one attention

World-actionread

Details
Overview

An omnimodal world model built as a mixture of transformers: a reasoner tower (the Qwen3-VL VLM) runs autoregressively over text and ViT tokens, and a generator tower denoises video latents, audio and action tokens with flow matching. The towers keep their own norms, attention projections and MLPs but share one self-attention operator, so every diffusion token can read the AR context. One set of weights serves generation, forward and inverse dynamics and a policy, selected by which tokens are clean and which are noisy; the DROID policy runs 4 steps with CFG split across 2 RTX Pro 6000 GPUs and skips video decoding.

Representation

Generation: Wan2.2-TI2V-5B VAE latents, 4x temporal and 32x32 spatial (16x16 VAE + 2x2 patch merge), linearly projected to the hidden size, so (H/32) x (W/32) tokens per latent frame [D]; understanding: ViT tokens (patch 16, 2x2 merge); audio 25 tokens/s [D: 48 kHz / hop 1920]

Core

Nano: 36 layers, hidden 4096, 32 heads / 8 KV heads of 128, FFN 12,288 in each of two towers = 16B (from Qwen3-VL-8B); Super: 64 layers, hidden 5120, 64 / 8 heads, FFN 25,600 = 64B; Edge 4B (28 layers, hidden 2048) not yet released

Attention

Shared self-attention: AR tokens attend causally to AR tokens only; DM tokens attend bidirectionally over all AR + DM tokens; AR tokens never read DM tokens; training packs a fixed 74,000-token context

Actions

Action vectors (relative ego pose 9-D, effector pose 9-D, grasp state; 10-D single arm up to 57-D egocentric human) enter as DM tokens through per-embodiment input and output projections; the MoT backbone is shared; policy adds a fresh action encoder, decoding MLP and action embedding tokens

Prediction

Flow matching: 50 steps for generation (guidance 6, shift 10), 4 steps for the DROID policy (guidance 3, shift 5) predicting 32 absolute joint-position actions at 15 Hz; the reasoner pass is computed once and cached across all steps; how σ enters the generator is not described

Decoder

Wan2.2 VAE decoder for video; skipped in policy serving, where only the action tokens are read

Memory

No streaming rollout is described: the generator is bidirectional over the whole packed context; paged KV caching only for reasoner serving (TensorRT-LLM / vLLM)

Speed

Nano 720p text-to-video on one GPU: 297 s on H100 NVL vs 115 s on B200 (PyTorch; frames and steps not stated); policy served on 2 RTX Pro 6000 with CFG parallelism, per-chunk latency not disclosed (company claims)

Key detail

Each token passes through one tower, so per-token compute stays near the dense 8B backbone while parameters double [D]; the policy runs 4 steps x a 540x640 three-view canvas and never decodes the video latents

Status and sources

company technical report. Availability: code + weights. Sources: Cosmos 3 technical report (22 Jun 2026) Sec. 2.1 (encoders, action tokenization), Sec. 2.3 (MoT, attention), Table 2 (variants), Sec. 4.2 (74K context), Sec. 5 (reasoner caching, CFG parallelism, Fig. 16 timings), Sec. 6.2.5 (DROID policy: 4 steps, 2 RTX Pro 6000, decoding skipped).

NVIDIA · 2026 · 2.6B

Hybrid linear DiT with a fixed-size state

State-spaceread

Details
Overview

A minute-scale camera-controlled world model whose DiT replaces most softmax attention with frame-wise Gated DeltaNet: 15 of 20 blocks keep a D×D recurrent state per head, updated once per latent frame, and only 5 blocks use softmax attention, run at deployment with an attention sink plus a local window. The LTX2 VAE packs 8 raw frames into one 128-channel latent frame, so 60 s of 720p fits one GPU. Self Forcing distillation gives a 4-step chunk-causal generator; with NVFP4 on one RTX 5090 it denoises 60 s of 720p in 34 s (authors).

Representation

LTX2 VAE, 128 latent channels, one latent frame per 8 raw frames; spatial stride and tokens per latent frame at 720p are not stated in the paper, which calls the representation 8x smaller than Wan2.1-VAE's

Core

Hybrid linear DiT from SANA-Video: 20 blocks, d 2240, 20 heads of 112; 15 frame-wise Gated DeltaNet blocks + softmax attention at layers {3, 7, 11, 15, 19}, keeping the original QKV and output projections; text, video and pose tokens pass through the alternating blocks; norm and modulation type not disclosed

Attention

GDN blocks: a D×D recurrent state per head updated once per latent frame from all S spatial tokens (forward scan global, reversed scan reset at chunk boundaries in the chunk-causal variant); softmax blocks: first latent frame as sink + local temporal window at deployment; chunk size not stated

Actions

6-DoF camera trajectory only, no keyboard: UCPE relative camera encoding on the geometric channels of a camera attention branch at latent-frame rate, plus the 8 raw-frame Plücker raymaps of one VAE stride packed into a 48-channel tensor through a zero-initialized 3D patch embedder; applied in every block

Prediction

Flow matching; 60-step chunk-causal AR generator distilled with Self Forcing to 4 steps; bidirectional, chunk-causal and distilled variants each run on one GPU

Decoder

LTX2 VAE decoder → 720p at 16 fps (961 frames = 60 s [D]); optional second stage: LTX-2 17B refiner with a rank-384 LoRA, 3 Euler steps

Memory

15 GDN layers hold 20 × 112² ≈ 0.25M values each, ≈7.5 MB in BF16 for all 15 [D]; the 5 softmax layers keep a sink + window KV, so memory is constant in rollout length (all-softmax runs out of memory at 60 s on an H100, Fig. 7b); no explicit 3D scene memory

Speed

60 s of 720p: DiT time on one H100 21.7 min at 60 steps → 43 s at 4 steps → 29 s with the sink; 34 s end to end on one RTX 5090 with NVFP4 (authors, Fig. 7a); 433 ms per denoising step at 720p on one H100, 5.68 GiB (Table 3, 5 s clips); 24.1 one-minute videos per hour on 8 H100s (Table 2)

Key detail

The only model in this gallery whose per-frame cost is constant in rollout length in 3/4 of its layers; the high-compression VAE is the bigger lever per step (3.4x latency, 8.9 → 5.4 GiB) and the softmax layers cost 1.17x per step [D]

Status and sources

arXiv preprint. Availability: code + weights. Sources: arXiv 2605.15178 abstract, Sec. 1, 3.1 (stages), 3.2 (frame-wise GDN, hybrid), 3.3 (UCPE + Plücker mixing), 5.1 (backbone), 5.4 and Fig. 7 (speed path), Tables 2-3, App. C.1 (head dim 112); abstract and title page state open-source with a GitHub link (weight release not verified here).

Skywork AI · 2026 · 5B

Bidirectional segment DiT with retrieved memory

Causal DiTread

Details
Overview

Skywork's 720p successor to Matrix-Game 2.0, built on Wan2.2-TI2V-5B. Unlike its predecessor it keeps a bidirectional DiT: each streaming segment denoises 10 new latent frames jointly with 4 past latents and 5 memory latents retrieved by camera pose and frustum overlap, all in one self-attention sequence with no KV cache. Multi-segment DMD distils it to 3 steps. The reported ~40 FPS at 720p needs 8 GPUs for the DiT plus 1 for the VAE, INT8 attention projections, a 75%-pruned decoder and GPU-side retrieval (company claim).

Representation

Wan2.2 VAE (4x16x16) + patchify; 880 tokens per 22x40 latent frame at 704x1280 if the patch is (1,2,2) as in Wan2.2 [D, assumption]; one latent frame = 4 video frames; 10 latent frames per segment ≈ 40 video frames [D]

Core

Wan2.2-TI2V-5B DiT (30 layers, d 3072, 24 heads, FFN 14336 per the HF config); action modules in the first 15 blocks as in Matrix-Game 2.0; teacher and student share one bidirectional architecture; a 28B MoE scale-up is also trained

Attention

Bidirectional within a segment: 5 retrieved memory latents + 4 past latents + 10 noisy current latents in one sequence (first segment: reference latent + 14 noisy latents), ≈16,720 tokens per segment [D]; head-wise perturbed RoPE bases; no KV cache

Actions

Keyboard actions through a dedicated cross-attention module, mouse signals through self-attention (Matrix-Game 2.0 design), in blocks 1-15; relative Plücker cues encode the camera geometry between the target and the retrieved memory

Prediction

Flow matching; multi-segment self-rollout DMD (1-6 segments, memory from an online pool) → 3 distilled steps per segment; error collection and injection train the model on its own imperfect histories

Decoder

MG-LightVAE: Wan2.2 decoder with reduced hidden widths (LightX2V-style), 50% or 75% pruned; decode 0.76 → 0.30 → 0.13 s per 17-frame 720x1280 clip (PSNR 33.79 → 31.84 → 31.14 dB); runs on its own GPU

Memory

Camera-aware retrieval: each query view takes the past frame with the highest frustum-overlap score (exact on CPU, approximate on GPU); the first latent can be kept as a persistent sink; without a KV cache the memory and past tokens are re-processed at every step

Speed

~40 FPS at 720p on an asynchronous 8+1 pipeline (8 DiT GPUs + 1 VAE GPU), GPU model not named (H-series with FlashAttention 3); leave-one-out Table 1: 27.38 FPS without INT8, 25.79 without MG-LightVAE, 6.60 with CPU retrieval; single-node 7+1 'slightly lower' (company claim); 3.1 one-minute videos/hour on 8 H100s in SANA-WM's benchmark (third party, config unstated); the ~40 FPS figure is a company claim

Key detail

Real time is a systems result: 9 GPUs, INT8 on the attention projections only (+46%), a 5.85x faster decoder (+55%) and GPU retrieval (≈6.1x); the authors say VAE decode is the bottleneck once the DiT is optimized

Status and sources

company technical report (arXiv), v3 Sep 2026. Availability: code + weights. Sources: verified_findings.md Findings 13-14 (8+1 pipeline, Table 1 FPS, Table 2 VAE times, INT8 scope, 3 steps); arXiv 2604.08995 Sec. 3.1 (base model, action injection), 3.2 (memory), 3.3 (multi-segment DMD), 3.4 (real-time inference), 5.1 (implementation: 4 past + 10 current + 5 memory latents), 5.2.3; HF Wan-AI/Wan2.2-TI2V-5B config.json (local copy: 30 layers, dim 3072, 24 heads, ffn 14336); SANA-WM arXiv 2605.15178 Table 2 (3.1 videos/hour on 8 H100s).

Mila, NYU · 2026 · ~15M total

One token per frame, CEM plans in under a second

Embedding predictorread

Details
Overview

The smallest JEPA world model in the gallery: a ViT-Tiny encoder and a 6-layer predictor trained end to end from pixels with two losses only (next-embedding MSE plus the SIGReg Gaussian regularizer), with no EMA, stop-gradient or frozen foundation encoder. Each frame is squeezed into a single 192-d [CLS] embedding, so the predictor sees at most 3 tokens, and a CEM plan of 300 samples x up to 30 iterations x horizon 5 finishes in 0.98 s against 47 s for DINO-WM.

Representation

One 192-d token per 224x224 frame: the last-layer [CLS] embedding of a ViT-Tiny (patch 14, 12 layers, 3 heads, width 192, ~5M) followed by a 1-layer MLP projector with BatchNorm

Core

Predictor: 6 layers, d 192, 16 heads of 64, MLP 2048, dropout 0.1, learned positional embeddings; ~10M; followed by a projector of the same design as the encoder's

Attention

Temporal causal mask over the history of frame embeddings; N = 3 frames (PushT, OGBench-Cube) or 1 (TwoRoom), i.e. at most 3 tokens per predictor call [D]

Actions

Zero-initialised AdaLN at every predictor layer; with frameskip 5 the 5 actions between frames form one 10-d action block, embedded to width 192

Prediction

One pass regresses the next frame embedding (MSE); encoder and predictor trained jointly, SIGReg keeps the embeddings Gaussian to prevent collapse

Decoder

None in training or planning; a diagnostic cross-attention decoder (196 queries → 224x224) only visualizes what the latent retains

Memory

Window of N = 3 frame embeddings; no KV cache

Speed

Full plan 0.98 s vs 47 s for DINO-WM, averaged over 50 runs (authors; GPU not stated); CEM with 300 samples, top 30, up to 30 iterations (PushT) or 10, horizon 5 latent steps = 25 environment steps, whole plan executed before replanning

Key detail

196x fewer tokens per frame than DINO-WM [D]; a PushT plan is 150 sequential batched calls (30 iterations x horizon 5) of ~18 GFLOP each [D], a latency-bound chain rather than a throughput job

Status and sources

arXiv preprint (v3 Jun 2026). Availability: code + weights. Sources: arXiv 2603.19312 Sec. 3 (architecture, planning), Sec. 4.2 and Fig. 3 (timing), App. D (encoder, predictor, decoder, planning solver); Hugging Face quentinll/lewm-pusht config.json (predictor d 192, head dim 64, MLP 2048, history 3; fetched); GitHub lucas-maes/le-wm README (checkpoints, code base).

Tsinghua IIIS, Galaxea AI · 2026 · 6B

Video DiT plus action expert, no imagined video

World-actionread

Details
Overview

A mixture-of-transformers world-action model that keeps video co-training but drops test-time imagination. A Wan2.2-5B video DiT and a 1B action-expert DiT (the same architecture at d 1024) share attention; in training, future video latents and the action chunk are denoised jointly under a structured mask, while at inference the video DiT runs once over the clean first-frame tokens and the action expert denoises a 32-step chunk in 10 steps. That gives 190 ms per chunk on one RTX 5090D against 810 ms for the imagine-then-execute variant of the same model.

Representation

Wan2.2 VAE latents of the observation, with the multi-camera images concatenated into one image; training video chunks of 9 frames after 4x temporal downsampling; tokens per frame not disclosed

Core

Video DiT from Wan2.2-5B (30 layers, d 3072, 24 heads, FFN 14,336 per its config.json) plus an action expert with the same architecture at d 1024 (1B); T5 text reaches all tokens through cross-attention; norms and timestep modulation not detailed in the paper

Attention

Shared attention with a structured mask: clean first-frame tokens attend to nothing else; future video tokens (training only) attend within the video branch and to the first frame; action tokens attend within the action branch and to the first frame, never to future video

Actions

Action chunk of h = 32 as tokens in the action expert, denoised by flow matching; at inference the expert reads the single-pass video features through the shared attention

Prediction

Training: joint flow matching over actions and future video latents (logit-normal t); inference: one video-DiT pass over the clean first frame, then 10 action denoising steps at CFG 1.0 (no second pass)

Decoder

None at deployment: no future video tokens are instantiated, denoised or decoded

Memory

Single-chunk policy; the outer autoregressive loop is omitted and no KV cache is described

Speed

190 ms per chunk on one RTX 5090D V2 32 GB (authors); the imagine-then-execute variant Fast-WAM-IDM takes 810 ms on the same GPU

Key detail

Removing test-time imagination costs little accuracy while removing video co-training costs much; the deployed graph is 1 pass of the 5B DiT plus 10 passes of the 1B expert [D]

Status and sources

arXiv preprint (v2 Mar 2026). Availability: closed. Sources: arXiv 2603.16666 Sec. 1, 3 (architecture, mask, inference), 4.1 (Wan2.2-5B, d_a 1024, h 32, 10 steps, CFG 1.0, RTX 5090D), 4.4 (190 vs 810 ms); Hugging Face Wan-AI/Wan2.2-TI2V-5B config.json (30 layers, d 3072, 24 heads, FFN 14336; fetched).

comma.ai · 2026 · 2B DiT + 150M compressor

Block-causal driving DiT that trains openpilot

Driving & robotsclaim

Details
Overview

The learned driving simulator behind openpilot 0.11, the first shipped driving policy trained entirely inside a world model. A ViT compressor turns the two camera views into a 32x16x32 latent, and a 2B block-causal diffusion transformer predicts the next frame latent from 2 s of context, 6-DoF relative-pose actions and 1 s of future frames (so it is also an inverse dynamics model). Sampling is frame by frame with 15 Euler steps and CFG 2.0; with KV caching comma reports 12.2 frames/s per GPU, a batched training-throughput number rather than an interactive latency.

Representation

ViT frame compressor (encoder 50M, decoder 100M, 2x deeper): two views (narrow, wide) of 3x128x256 → one 32x16x32 latent; tokens per frame after DiT patching not stated (512 if one token per 16x32 cell [D, assumption])

Core

2B diffusion transformer: 48 layers, d 1600, 25 heads (n_layer=48, n_head=25, n_embd=1600), 'adapted to 3 dimensional data'; norm and MLP details not disclosed

Attention

Block-causal in every layer: tokens attend to their own frame and past frames; a sample = 2 s past context + 1 s future conditioning + 0-7 s simulation window at 5 fps (10 context frames [D])

Actions

6-DoF relative positions, diffusion noise level and frame indices injected via AdaLN-single (PixArt-α style)

Prediction

Rectified flow with logit-normal noise sampling; frame by frame, 15 Euler steps, classifier-free guidance 2.0 (up to 30 DiT passes per frame if the conditional and unconditional branches run separately [D]); noise-level augmentation for rollout robustness

Decoder

ViT decoder (100M) → narrow and wide 128x256 frames

Memory

KV cache enabled by the block-causal mask; context 2 s at 5 fps

Speed

12.2 frames/s per GPU throughput with KV caching (company claim; GPU type not stated); ≈366 DiT frame-evaluations per second per GPU at 15 steps × CFG, i.e. batched over rollouts [D]

Key detail

Low-resolution, 5 fps latents make a 2B DiT cheap enough to generate the policy's whole training set; trained on 2.5M minutes (≈41,700 h [D]) of driving video; weights release not stated on the page

Status and sources

blog post. Availability: closed. Sources: blog.comma.ai/011release (17 Mar 2026): sections Frame Compressor, Diffusion Transformer, sampling and throughput; ar_token_and_physical_ai.md Group 2 (derived counts).

NVIDIA · 2026 · 14B

One 14B DiT denoises video and actions together

World-actionread

Details
Overview

A 14B world-action model: the Wan2.1-I2V-14B image-to-video DiT is fully fine-tuned into a chunk-wise autoregressive flow-matching model that denoises the next 2 latent frames of video and the matching 1.6 s action chunk together, with one shared timestep and separate output decoders. Clean context sits in a KV cache of at most 8 latent frames, and after each chunk executes the predicted frames are replaced by encoded real observations. Naive inference costs 5.7 s per chunk; CFG on 2 GPUs, velocity caching (16 → 4 steps), compilation, NVFP4 and the 1-step DreamZero-Flash schedule bring it to 150 ms on 2 GB200.

Representation

Frozen Wan2.1 VAE latents (480p model); multi-view inputs tiled into one frame; 8 latent frames = 33 raw frames (4x temporal); tokens per latent frame not disclosed

Core

Wan2.1-I2V-14B-480P DiT with all blocks fine-tuned: 40 layers, d 5120, 40 heads, FFN 13,824 (base config.json); only state and action encoders plus an action decoder are added; text encoder, image encoder and VAE stay frozen; block internals not detailed in the paper (LayerNorm and RoPE named in its quantization notes)

Attention

Chunk-causal: the noisy current chunk (K = 2 latent frames + its action chunk) attends to the clean previous chunks; frames inside a chunk share one timestep; max context 8 latent frames (4 chunks) = 6.6 s

Actions

Action latents denoised jointly with the video in the same DiT, same timestep; chunks of 48 actions at 30 Hz (AgiBot) or 24 at 15 Hz (DROID) = 1.6 s; proprioceptive state through a state encoder; relative joint positions, Savitzky-Golay smoothed; state-encoder entry point not detailed

Prediction

Flow matching: 16 steps baseline → 4 effective with velocity caching (cached velocity reused when cosine similarity exceeds a threshold) → 1 step with DreamZero-Flash (video timesteps biased to high noise, t = 1 − Beta(7,1); action timesteps uniform)

Decoder

Wan VAE decoder for the predicted video; control does not need it, since predicted frames are replaced by encoded real frames (paper does not say whether video is decoded at deployment)

Memory

KV cache bounded at 8 latent frames; refreshed with VAE-encoded real observations after every chunk

Speed

5.7 s per chunk naive on one GPU; 9.6x on one H100 (~0.59 s [D]); 16.6x with NVFP4 (~350 ms at 4 steps) and 38x with Flash (150 ms at 1 step, ~7 Hz) on 2 GB200 with CFG split across the GPUs (company claims, Tables 1 and 3)

Key detail

Generating actions only does not help at 14B (steps x blocks dominate); the 38x comes from step count (16 → 1), 2-GPU CFG, CUDA graphs and NVFP4 (E2M1 weights and activations, FP8 QKV and softmax)

Status and sources

arXiv preprint (company). Availability: code + weights. Sources: arXiv 2602.15922 Sec. 3 (architecture, inference), Sec. 3.2 (optimizations), Table 1 (speedups), Table 3 (Flash), Sec. 4 (training), App. C (chunking, context), App. D (CFG parallelism, caching, NVFP4); Hugging Face Wan-AI/Wan2.1-I2V-14B-480P config.json (40 layers, d 5120, 40 heads, FFN 13824; fetched).

Robbyant · 2026 · 14B dense

Causal Wan DiT that keeps the whole rollout in KV

Causal DiTread

Details
Overview

The largest open real-time world model: the high-noise expert of the Wan2.2 I2V A14B mixture (28B in total, 14B active) is adapted to block-causal attention and distilled with DMD plus an adversarial head to 4 steps. Camera rotation (Plücker) and W/A/S/D keys enter through adaptive normalization in adapter layers. By default it keeps the full KV cache of the whole rollout, so memory is emergent from context, but the cache grows by about 3.4 GB per 12-frame chunk and throughput falls from 8.9 to 3.6 FPS over a minute (WorldKV, 4×B200). The company claims 16 fps at 480p on one 8-GPU node.

Representation

Wan 3D causal VAE, stride 4x8x8; patch (1,2,2) → 1,560 tokens per 30x52 latent frame at 480x832 [D]; chunk = 3 latent frames = 4,680 tokens = 12 output frames [D]

Core

Wan2.2 I2V A14B config: 40 layers, d 5120, 40 heads, FFN 13824; the Fast model is initialized from the high-noise expert alone, a dense 14B causal DiT (the base runs two 14B experts, one active per timestep)

Attention

Block-causal: bidirectional within a chunk, causal across chunks, KV cache; local_attn_size -1 and sink_size 0 by default = full KV over the whole rollout (window and sink exist as flags)

Actions

Camera rotation as Plücker embeddings concatenated with multi-hot W/A/S/D keys → Plücker encoder → AdaLN scale and shift in the DiT blocks; in that stage only the action adapters and AdaLN parameters are trained

Prediction

DMD with self-rollout plus an adversarial head on the fake-score network (APT-style, no R1/R2); 4 steps at timestep indices [0, 179, 358, 679] with shift 5 (code); the bidirectional base samples 70 steps

Decoder

Wan VAE decoder → 12 frames per chunk at 480x832 (checkpoints also support 720p)

Memory

No memory module: 'an emergent ability derived from the context window'; full KV ≈3.4 GB per 3-latent-frame chunk and >200 GB per minute (WorldKV; ≈3.8 GB per chunk by my count [D])

Speed

16 fps at 480p with <1 s latency on one GPU node (company claim; release script uses 8 GPUs with Ulysses sequence parallelism, GPU type not stated); WorldKV on 4×B200: 8.87 → 3.61 FPS over a one-minute rollout with full KV, 3.83 FPS average vs 8.10 with a sliding window (4×H200: 2.36 vs 5.05)

Key detail

Attention, not the GEMMs, sets the decay: after one minute each pass attends to ≈374k cached keys, ≈1.4 PFLOP of attention against ≈112 TFLOP of linear work per pass [D]

Status and sources

arXiv preprint (company), Jan 2026. Availability: code + weights. Sources: arXiv 2601.20540 Sec. 3.1.3, 3.3 (action injection), 3.4 (causal adaptation, DMD + adversarial), 4.1, 6.2; lingbot-world code: wan/configs/wan_i2v_A14B.py (40 layers, dim 5120, 40 heads, ffn 13824, 70 steps); wan/image2video_fast.py (timesteps_index, local_attn_size -1, sink_size 0, chunk_size 3); run_fast.sh (8 GPUs, ulysses 8); HF robbyant/lingbot-world-fast model card (16 fps, <1 s latency, Apache-2.0); WorldKV arXiv 2605.22718 Sec. 1, Table 1, Fig. 2.

Robbyant · 2026 · 5.3B

Interleaves video and actions in one causal sequence

World-actionread

Details
Overview

A causal world-action model that interleaves video latents and actions in one autoregressive sequence with a KV cache. Two parallel transformer streams of the same depth, a 5B video stream initialised from Wan2.2-5B (d 3072) and a 0.35B action stream (d 768), are joined by shared attention. Each step denoises the next chunk of 4 latent frames with 3 Euler steps only to s = 0.6 (partial denoising, enabled by noisy-history augmentation), then decodes the 16 actions as inverse dynamics in 10 steps; real observations re-enter the cache in closed loop.

Representation

Wan2.2 causal VAE (4x16x16) plus 2x patchify; all camera views concatenated along the width → 192 spatial tokens per latent frame; video at 12.5 Hz with 4 actions per frame (50 Hz)

Core

MoT: video stream from Wan2.2-5B, 30 layers, d 3072 (24 heads, FFN 14,336 per the Wan2.2-TI2V-5B config); action stream of the same depth at d 768 (~350M), initialised by interpolating the video weights scaled by sqrt(d_v/d_a); RoPE in both; T5 text through cross-attention (which stream reads it is not stated); norms and timestep modulation not detailed

Attention

Causal over the interleaved video-action sequence (teacher forcing), bidirectional inside a chunk; action tokens are projected to d 3072 for the joint attention and back; training packs episodes into sequences of up to 10K tokens

Actions

Action tokens in the sequence (single-layer MLP encoder and decoder, hidden 256; quantile-normalised), decoded by inverse dynamics conditioned on the predicted visual transition; chunk K = 4 frames = 16 actions [D]

Prediction

Flow matching with an Euler solver: video 3 steps to s = 0.6 (partial denoising) at CFG 5.0, actions 10 steps to s = 1.0 at CFG 1.0; a forward-dynamics step re-grounds the cache on the latest real frame

Decoder

Wan2.2 VAE decoder exists for visualisation, but actions are read from latents and the partially denoised video is never decoded for control

Memory

Causal KV cache over the interleaved history; the asynchronous pipeline keeps only the last executed chunk, the latest real frame, the executing chunk and its forecast

Speed

Not disclosed: no latency, control rate or GPU is given; the authors name video-token denoising as the primary inference bottleneck

Key detail

Per step: 3 video steps x 2 CFG passes = 6 passes of the 5B stream over 768 new tokens, plus 10 passes of the 0.35B stream [D]

Status and sources

arXiv preprint (v2 Mar 2026). Availability: code + weights. Sources: arXiv 2601.21998 Sec. 1, 3.2-3.4 (interleaving, MoT block, noisy-history augmentation, KV cache, async pipeline), Sec. 4.2 (dimensions, VAE, 192 tokens, sampling), Sec. 4 (12.5 Hz video / 50 Hz actions); Hugging Face Wan-AI/Wan2.2-TI2V-5B config.json (30 layers, d 3072, 24 heads, FFN 14336; fetched).

NVIDIA · 2026 · 2B

Video DiT predicts actions as extra latent frames

World-actionread

Details
Overview

Cosmos-Predict2-2B Video2World, a latent video diffusion transformer over Wan2.1 VAE latents, fully fine-tuned into a robot policy with no architectural change. Proprioception, the action chunk and the value are injected as extra latent frames: blank images are VAE-encoded and their latents overwritten with tiled copies of the vectors, so the denoising process that predicts future images also predicts actions. As a direct policy it denoises everything in parallel in 5 steps (0.61 s per chunk on one H100) and discards the future state and value; planning mode decodes them autoregressively for best-of-N search.

Representation

Wan2.1 VAE latent frames (8x spatial, 4x temporal, 16 channels); one latent frame per modality and camera view, e.g. 9 for LIBERO (blank, proprio, 2 views, action chunk, future proprio, 2 future views, value) or 11 with 3 cameras; each image is repeated 4x so one latent frame is one timestep; LIBERO data at 224 px per the repo config, i.e. ~196 tokens per latent frame with the 2x2 patch [D]

Core

Cosmos-Predict2-2B Video2World DiT, all weights fine-tuned: 28 blocks, d 2048, 16 heads, patch 2x2x1, 3D RoPE, AdaLN-LoRA timestep conditioning (repo net config COSMOS_V1_2B); T5 text via cross-attention; no new modules; Predict1 block design with QK RMSNorm

Attention

Bidirectional 3D self-attention over all latent frames; clean conditioning frames (current state) and noisy target frames share the sequence

Actions

The action chunk (K x d_act, scaled to [-1, 1], flattened and duplicated to fill H' x W' x C') overwrites a placeholder latent frame and is read back by averaging the copies; K = 16 (LIBERO, all executed), 32 (RoboCasa, 16 executed), 50 at 25 Hz (ALOHA)

Prediction

EDM denoising with sigma_max 80 and sigma_min 4: 5 steps (LIBERO, RoboCasa) or 10 (ALOHA) with action, future state and value in parallel, the latter two discarded; planning: autoregressive 10 + 5 + 5 steps, ensembles of 3 states and 5 values, best-of-N = 8

Decoder

Wan2.1 VAE decoder only to visualise predicted future images; actions and values are read from the latents without any decoding

Memory

None: the input is the current observation only, no history; 6.0-8.9 GB VRAM at inference (README)

Speed

Per action chunk on one H100 (authors): 0.61 s at 5 steps, 0.95 s at 10, 0.16 s at 1 step (RoboCasa still 66.4% success at 1 step); best-of-8 planning 4.9 s on 8 parallel H100s

Key detail

Every step also denoises the future-image and value frames the policy throws away; latency is roughly 68 ms per step plus 0.27 s fixed [D: from 0.61 s at 5 and 0.95 s at 10 steps]

Status and sources

ICLR 2026. Availability: code + weights. Sources: arXiv 2601.16163 Sec. 3 (base model, VAE), 4.1 (latent frame injection), 4.2 (parallel vs AR decoding), App. A.1 (injection details), A.2 (action chunks, training), A.3.1 and A.4.2 (steps, latency); GitHub NVlabs/cosmos-policy README (VRAM), net.py (COSMOS_V1_2B: 2048 channels, 28 blocks, 16 heads, patch 2, rope3d, adaln_lora 256) and cosmos_policy_experiment_configs.py (resolution 224, state_t 9; fetched).

Tencent Hunyuan · 2025 · 8B

Causal DiT with memory retrieved by camera view

Causal DiTread

Details
Overview

Tencent's real-time interactive world model: the HunyuanVideo-1.5 MM-DiT made chunk-wise block-causal (4 latent frames = 16 video frames per chunk) and distilled with Context Forcing to 4 steps. Each chunk attends to a memory rebuilt from the 3 most recent chunks plus 1 chunk retrieved by field-of-view overlap and camera distance, with RoPE indices re-assigned so old frames look recent. Keys enter through the timestep embedding, camera pose through a relative encoding inside attention. The company's 24 FPS at 720p needs 8 H800 GPUs with token parallelism, quantization and streaming VAE decode.

Representation

HunyuanVideo-1.5 causal 3D VAE: 16x spatial, 4x temporal, 32 channels; patch 1x1x1 → 3,600 tokens per latent frame at 720p, 14,400 per 4-latent chunk of 16 frames [D]

Core

HunyuanVideo-1.5 480P-I2V transformer: 54 double-stream MM-DiT blocks, d 2048, 16 heads, MLP ratio 4 (HF config); the paper describes each block as 3D self-attention + cross-attention + FFN with timestep adaLN; 8B per the README (a 5B Wan-based variant is lighter but weaker); activation not disclosed

Attention

Block-causal over chunks with a KV cache; context = 3 temporal + 1 spatial memory chunk = 57,600 tokens at 720p [D]; first chunk kept as an attention sink; temporal reframing re-assigns RoPE indices so a retrieved chunk sits at a small relative distance

Actions

Dual representation: discrete keys → PE + zero-initialized MLP added to the timestep embedding (adaLN); camera pose → PRoPE relative encoding in a second attention term, output = Attn1 + zero_init(Attn2)

Prediction

Flow matching; Context Forcing distillation (memory-augmented bidirectional teacher, DMD loss) from 100 NFE to 4 denoising steps per 16-frame chunk

Decoder

HunyuanVideo-1.5 VAE decoder → 16 frames per chunk; progressive decode in small batches streamed over Triton, parallelized over 8 GPUs; the open checkpoints are 480P

Memory

Reconstituted context memory rebuilt per chunk by FOV-overlap and camera-distance retrieval from past chunks; no explicit 3D state; KV ≈25.5 GB in BF16 for the 57,600-token context, ≈3.2 GB per GPU when split 8 ways [D]

Speed

24 FPS at 720p on 8×H800 (company claim); Table 4: 2.80 → 3.80 (DiT parallelism + quantization) → 16.0 (+VAE) → 24.0 FPS (+streaming decode); 4.95 FPS for the 8B model on 4×H200 (measured by WorldKV); 28 GB per GPU at sp=8 (README)

Key detail

Distillation cuts passes 25x, but the remaining 8.57x to real time is systems work; ≈85% of per-chunk FLOPs is attention against the 72,000-token sequence [D]

Status and sources

arXiv preprint (ICML 2026 format), v2 Jun 2026. Availability: code + weights. Sources: arXiv 2512.14614 Sec. 3.1-3.5, Table 4, App. A, Table 8; HF tencent/HunyuanVideo-1.5 transformer/480p_i2v/config.json and vae/config.json (local copies); HY-WorldPlay README (8B HY Video / 5B Wan lines, 480P checkpoints, GPU memory at sp=8); WorldKV arXiv 2605.22718 Table 1 (4.95 FPS on 4×H200).

NVIDIA · 2025 · 2B and 14B

Bidirectional DiT that generates whole video clips

Driving & robotsread

Details
Overview

NVIDIA's physical-AI world foundation model: a flow-matching DiT that generates a whole 93-frame clip (24 latent frames, 5.8 s at 16 fps) with full self-attention, unifying Text2World, Image2World and Video2World by replacing conditioning frames in the sequence and flagging them with a mask token. The Cosmos-Reason1 VLM replaces T5 as the text encoder. It is a clip generator, not an interactive model: no action input in the base model (an action-conditioned robot variant exists), no KV cache, rCM distillation to 4 steps, and no inference speed reported.

Representation

Wan2.1 causal VAE (4x8x8) + 1x2x2 patchify; 3,520 tokens per 44x80 latent frame at 1280x704, 84,480 tokens per 93-frame clip of 24 latent frames [D]

Core

2B: 32 layers, d 2048, FFN 8192, 16 heads of 128; 14B: 36 layers, d 5120, FFN 20480, 40 heads; AdaLN-LoRA (rank 256) timestep modulation, 3D RoPE, GELU; blocks of self-attention, cross-attention and MLP

Attention

Full (bidirectional) self-attention over all tokens of the clip; training at 720p/93 frames needs context parallelism 2 (2B) or 8 (14B)

Actions

None in the base model: conditioning is text (Cosmos-Reason1 multi-block activations projected to 1024-d, via cross-attention) and 1 or 5 conditioning frames concatenated with a mask-token flag; a 2B robot/action-cond variant and 7-camera driving variants exist (mechanism not read)

Prediction

Flow matching; rCM (continuous-time consistency + distribution matching) distillation to 4 steps, 2B overall score 0.768 → 0.764 (Table 7); teacher step count not located

Decoder

Wan2.1 VAE decoder → 93 frames at up to 1280x704

Memory

None: clip-level generation; longer videos by chaining Video2World with 5 conditioning frames; no KV cache

Speed

Not disclosed; training MFU 36.49% (2B) and 33.08% (14B) on 4,096 H100s at 720p/93 frames (Table 9); ≈3.4e14 dense FLOPs per 2B pass over 84,480 tokens, before attention [D]

Key detail

A bidirectional whole-clip DiT with ≈84k-token attention per pass is the template the causal game models in this gallery were built to escape; the shipped acceleration lever is 4-step rCM distillation

Status and sources

company technical report (arXiv 2511.00062, v2 Feb 2026). Availability: code + weights. Sources: arXiv 2511.00062 Sec. 3.1-3.2 (Table 3 configs, tokenizer, text encoder, Fig. 2), 4.2.1 (frame replacement, mask token), 4.2.3 (rCM, Table 7), 4.3 and Table 9 (MFU, context parallelism); NVIDIA research page (local src/pred25.txt) for the released-model list; ar_token_and_physical_ai.md Group 2 (derived token counts, assuming 1280x704 for 720p as in Predict1).

Google DeepMind · 2025 · 1.6B + 400M tokenizer

Few-step space-time transformer with agent heads

Causal DiTverified

Details
Overview

A scalable world model that trains a Minecraft agent entirely offline inside its own imagination. A 400M block-causal transformer tokenizer (masked autoencoding, continuous tanh bottleneck) turns each 360x640 frame into 256 spatial tokens of 32 channels, and a 1.6B block-causal dynamics transformer, factorized over space and time with temporal attention in every 4th layer and GQA, denoises the next frame's tokens with a shortcut-forcing objective in K = 4 passes. The context is 192 frames (9.6 s), the model runs at 21 FPS on one H100, and policy, reward and value heads read agent tokens inside the same transformer.

Representation

256 spatial tokens x 32 channels per frame (a 512x16 bottleneck reshaped) from a 400M block-causal MAE tokenizer with a continuous tanh bottleneck; 384x640 padded input = 960 patches of 16x16

Core

1.6B dynamics transformer: pre-RMSNorm, RoPE, SwiGLU, QKNorm, attention logit soft-capping; layer, head and width counts not disclosed in the paper

Attention

Block-causal: all tokens of a frame attend to each other and to the past; space-only and time-only layers, temporal attention every 4th layer, GQA; context 192 frames = 49,152 spatial tokens [D]

Actions

Interleaved tokens: each action component (mouse, keyboard) is encoded into S_a tokens and summed with a learned embedding; each frame block also carries S_r registers and one shortcut signal-level/step-size token

Prediction

Shortcut forcing (diffusion forcing + shortcut models, x-prediction, ramp loss weight): K = 4 passes per frame instead of 64, no separate distillation; context frames re-noised at tau_ctx = 0.1

Decoder

The tokenizer's block-causal transformer decoder, frame by frame, to 360x640

Memory

KV cache over 192 frames (9.6 s); size not computable from the disclosed numbers; the authors name MLP FLOPs and KV-cache bandwidth as the inference limits

Speed

21 FPS at 640x360 on one H100 (authors, Table 1); the design cascade runs 0.8 → 9.1 (4-step shortcut) → 18.9 (temporal attention every 4 layers) → 23.2 (GQA) → 21.4 FPS at 256 tokens (Table 2)

Key detail

Agent tokens attend to everything but nothing attends back to them, so policy, reward and value heads share the world model's trunk; the transformer stays frozen during imagination training

Status and sources

arXiv preprint. Availability: closed. Sources: verified_findings Findings 7-10 (arXiv 2509.24527 Sec. 3.2-3.4, Sec. 4, App. A, Tables 1-2); arXiv 2509.24527 Sec. 3.1 (tokenizer), 3.3 (agent tokens, heads), 3.4 (efficient transformer); arxiv.org/html/2509.24527 fetched for layer and head counts: none given.

Meta FAIR · 2025 · 32B

Code LLM trained to predict execution traces

LLM & coderead

Details
Overview

A 32B dense decoder-only LLM mid-trained on observation-action trajectories: Python execution traces (stack-frame locals after each executed line) and agentic Docker sessions. The same transformer is policy and world model; a world-model step is ordinary text generation of the next observation. For compute it is plain long-context LLM decoding, kept affordable by GQA and a 3:1 mix of 8k local and 131k global sliding-window layers that caps the KV cache at about 9.5 GiB [D].

Representation

Text and code tokens, Llama 3 BPE tokenizer, vocabulary 128,256; an observation is the stack-frame locals as JSON, an action is the Python line executed (custom separator tokens)

Core

Dense decoder-only: 64 layers, d 6144, FFN 21,504 (SwiGLU), 48 query heads of 128, 8 KV heads (GQA), RMSNorm pre-norm; 32B parameters

Attention

Document-causal; local sliding window 8,192 tokens and global window 131,072 tokens interleaved 3:1 (48 local + 16 global layers [D]); scaled RoPE, θ 1M, scale factor 16

Actions

Actions are text in the stream (a Python statement or an agent tool call); the next observation is generated as text after it

Prediction

Next-token softmax over 128k vocabulary; one pass per token, so one trace step costs as many passes as the JSON frame has tokens

Decoder

None; the output is text (trace frames, code, tool calls)

Memory

KV cache per token per layer 4 KiB in bf16 (8 KV heads × 128); at 131k context ~8 GiB for the 16 global layers + ~1.5 GiB for the 48 local layers ≈ 9.5 GiB, vs 32 GiB if all layers were global [D]; FastGen serving with paged attention and host-side KV cache

Speed

No decode-throughput figure; inference fits one 80 GB H100 with quantization (authors; bf16 weights alone are 64 GB [D]); trained on 2,048 H100s for pre- and mid-training (Table 3)

Key detail

13T training tokens, 5T of them world-model mid-training at 131k context; the world model is the LLM itself, so acceleration means long-context, memory-bound decoding

Status and sources

arXiv preprint (open weights). Availability: code + weights. Sources: arXiv 2510.02387 Sec. 2.2 (trace format), Sec. 4.1 and Table 2 (architecture), Fig. 6a (3:1 layer pattern); arXiv 2510.02387 Sec. 1 (single H100 with quantization), Sec. 6 Table 3 (training GPUs), Sec. 6.2 (FastGen); research_notes rl_llm_objectcentric_ssm.md Sec. 2 (KV-cache arithmetic).

A real-time interactive game world model: a Wan-style video diffusion transformer made block-causal and distilled with DMD Self-Forcing to 3 denoising steps per 12-frame chunk. Actions

Prediction

DMD Self-Forcing distillation; 3 steps per chunk (timesteps 1000, 666, 333)

Decoder

Wan2.1 VAE decoder with a decode cache; 12 video frames per chunk

Rolling KV cache, oldest evicted, no sink; ~0.97 GB at batch 1 [D]; a 9-frame cache produced artifacts earlier

About 41% of the 40 ms frame budget does not shrink with fewer steps (VAE decode and other fixed work) [D]

AgiBot · 2025 · 2B + 160M action decoder

Thin action DiT reads a video DiT's cached latents

World-actionread

Details
Overview

A two-stream world-action model on top of GE-Base, an instruction-conditioned multi-view video DiT built from LTX-Video 2B and pretrained on ~3,000 h of AgiBot-World-Beta. GE-Act adds a parallel 160M action branch with the same depth but a smaller hidden size; it reads the visual latents of every GE-Base block through cross-attention and denoises a 54-step action trajectory by flow matching. At deployment the video DiT runs a single denoising step whose latents are cached, the action branch runs 5 steps, and a 54-step trajectory comes out in 200 ms on a robot-mounted RTX 4090.

Representation

Frozen video VAE latents of three views (head, left wrist, right wrist); initial frame plus 4 sparse memory frames per view; GE-Base-LF maps 9-frame clips at 5 Hz to 2 latent frames; tokens per frame not disclosed

Core

GE-Base: LTX-Video 2B DiT (28 layers, 32 heads of 64 = d 2048 per its config.json) with 2D RoPE plus view embeddings, cross-view attention in selected blocks and a causal cross-view block; GE-Act: same block design and depth with a reduced hidden size, 160M parameters (width not stated); norms and modulation not detailed

Attention

Video: spatial self-attention per view, cross-view self-attention over (views, H, W) in sparse blocks, T5-XXL instruction via cross-attention; GE-Act action tokens cross-attend to the visual latents of every GE-Base block

Actions

54-step trajectories at 30 Hz (dual-arm 14-D end-effector poses) denoised by flow matching from noise-initialised action tokens; a new action DiT is trained from scratch for each new embodiment

Prediction

Slow-fast asynchronous inference: 1 flow-matching step of the video DiT with its latents cached, then 5 action denoising steps on that cache; video DiT at 5 Hz vs action model at 30 Hz (1:6)

Decoder

Frozen video VAE decoder, used only when GE-Base generates video (GE-Sim); GE-Act never produces pixels

Memory

Sparse memory: 4 frames sampled from earlier chunks, concatenated with the initial frame per view

Speed

54-step trajectory in 200 ms on an onboard RTX 4090 mounted on the robot (authors), i.e. 5 chunks/s [D]; training: GE-Base-MR 32 A100 x ~7 days, GE-Base-LF 32 A100 x ~3 days, GE-Act pretraining 16 A100 x ~3 days

Key detail

Partial video denoising in deployment: one 2B video pass plus 5 passes of a thin action DiT [D]; the only model in this set timed on a single robot-mounted consumer GPU

Status and sources

ICLR 2026. Availability: code + weights. Sources: arXiv 2508.05635 Sec. 2.1 (GE-Base architecture, views, attention), 2.2 (MR/LF stages, training hardware), 3.1 (GE-Act, 160M), 3.2 (action training), 3.3 (slow-fast inference, 200 ms), Sec. 4 (new embodiments); Hugging Face Lightricks/LTX-Video transformer/config.json (28 layers, 32 heads x 64; fetched); ICLR 2026 page (venue; code and models promised, release not verified here).

Details
Overview

A Dreamer-style agent with a spatial latent state. A CNN VAE encodes each 64x64 frame as a 4x4 grid of 32-way categoricals in 32 groups, a temporal transformer with one token per step carries the history, and a small spatial MaskGIT transformer predicts the next 4x4 grid in S = 3 parallel refinement passes instead of 16 serial token decodes. 4x4 spatial grid x 32 groups x 32 classes per 64x64 frame from a CNN categorical VAE; 16 spatial tokens per step

Core

Temporal transformer: 4 blocks, d 512; spatial MaskGIT predictor: 2 blocks, d 256 over 16 tokens; 8 heads, dropout 0.1; 30M parameters in total; block internals not disclosed

Attention

Temporal: causal masked self-attention with relative positions, context 64 steps; spatial: bidirectional over the 4x4 grid

Actions

Action mixer MLP (as in STORM) concatenates the one-hot action with the 512-d latent features before the temporal transformer

Prediction

Next 4x4 grid by MaskGIT with a cosine mask schedule: S = 3 passes per imagined step; S = 1 or a plain MLP head runs at 33 FPS but scores lower

CNN decoder from z_t and h_t for training; the actor-critic learns in latent space, so nothing is decoded in imagination

Memory

Cached keys and values over the 64-step context, carried from one batch to the next (TBTT)

16 spatial tokens per step predicted in 3 parallel passes instead of 16 serial ones; two small transformers, one over time and one over space

Alibaba DAMO Academy · 2025 · ~7B

One LLM writes next-frame and action tokens

World-actionread

Details
Overview

A single autoregressive transformer, initialised from Chameleon, that treats images, text and actions as one token vocabulary: it predicts the next frame's VQ-GAN codes as a world model and the next action's 7 tokens as a VLA, and training both together improves both. There are no diffusion steps; everything is next-token decoding, so an action costs 7 serial passes and an imagined frame 256 or 1,024. A custom mask hides the earlier actions of a chunk so that each action depends only on text and images, which lets the chunk be generated in parallel.

Representation

VQ-GAN image tokenizer (compression 16, codebook 8192): 256 tokens per 256x256 frame or 1,024 per 512x512; BPE text; one shared vocabulary of 65,536 including the 8192 image and 256 action tokens

Core

Chameleon-initialised decoder-only LLM; the paper gives no size, the released base_model config.json has 32 layers, d 4096, 32 heads, FFN 11,008 (~7B; 14 GB of bf16 safetensors [D]); block details not disclosed in the paper

Attention

Causal over text, image and action tokens in world-model mode; in action mode a mask lets each action attend to text and images but not to earlier actions of the chunk; default M = 2 input frames

Actions

7 discrete tokens per action (3 relative positions, 3 relative angles, 1 gripper), 256 bins per dimension; chunks of K = 5 (K = 10 on LIBERO-Long)

Prediction

Next-token softmax; 7 tokens per action, and the masked chunk can be generated in parallel (authors); 256 or 1,024 serial passes per generated frame

Decoder

VQ-GAN decoder for predicted image tokens (world-model mode); actions need no decoding

Memory

LLM KV cache over the prompt (history frames + text); 1, 2 or 4 history frames evaluated, 2 by default

Speed

LIBERO, GPU not stated (authors, Table 5): 2.27 / 1.77 / 1.22 FPS with 1 / 2 / 4 history frames without chunking, 3.67 / 3.13 / 2.78 FPS with chunking

Key detail

An LLM-style decode workload, token-serial and memory-bandwidth-bound, the opposite profile from the diffusion WAMs; each imagined frame is 256 to 1,024 decode steps

Status and sources

arXiv preprint. Availability: code + weights. Sources: arXiv 2506.21539 Sec. 3.2 (tokenizers, Chameleon init), 3.3 (attention mask), 4.1 (M = 2, K), 4.3 and Table 5 (history length, FPS); Hugging Face Alibaba-DAMO-Academy/WorldVLA base_model/config.json (32 layers, hidden 4096, 32 heads, FFN 11008, vocab 65536; fetched) and file sizes (2 safetensors, 14.0 GB); GitHub alibaba-damo-academy/WorldVLA README (now RynnVLA-002; LIBERO checkpoints).

Adobe Research and UT Austin · 2025 · 1.3B

Few-step causal Wan DiT trained on its own rollouts

Causal DiTread

Details
Overview

The distillation recipe behind most real-time game world models (Matrix-Game 2.0, LongLive, SANA-WM). It converts the bidirectional Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B flow-matching DiT into a block-causal autoregressive model, trains it by rolling out its own 4-step generations with a KV cache and matching the teacher's distribution (DMD), and keeps a rolling KV cache of 21 latent frames at inference. It is text-to-video only, with no action input. The authors report 17 FPS at 832x480 on one H100 with 0.69 s first-frame latency.

Representation

Wan2.1 causal 3D VAE latents (stride 4x8x8, 16 channels); patch (1,2,2) → 1,560 tokens per 30x52 latent frame at 832x480 [D]; 81 frames = 21 latent frames

Core

Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B DiT: 30 layers, d 1536, 12 heads of 128, FFN 8960; umT5 text via cross-attention; 1.3B, unchanged from the base; the 14B model serves only as the frozen DMD teacher

Attention

Block-causal: dense within a 3-latent-frame chunk (4,680 tokens), causal across chunks; context 21 latent frames = 32,760 tokens; with the KV cache, inference uses dense FlashAttention-3, no mask kernel

Actions

None; text prompt only (umT5 cross-attention, 512-token KV cache per layer)

Prediction

Flow matching distilled with DMD Self Forcing to 4 steps (1000, 750, 500, 250; shift 5); the released loop adds 1 pass at timestep 0 per chunk to write clean KV, so 5 DiT passes per 12-frame chunk [D]

Decoder

Wan2.1 VAE decoder → 12 frames per chunk at 832x480; decoding is ≈32% of pipeline time after distillation (Flash-VAED Table 9)

Memory

Rolling KV cache of the most recent 21 latent frames, oldest evicted: O(TL) vs O(L²+TL) for recomputing overlaps; ≈6.0 GB in BF16 at batch 1 [D]; trained not to attend to the first chunk so the rolling cache does not flicker

Speed

17.0 FPS, 0.69 s latency (chunk-wise) and 8.9 FPS, 0.45 s (frame-wise) at 832x480 on one H100 (authors, Table 1); 16.1 FPS on 10 s videos with the rolling cache vs 4.6 FPS with KV recomputation

Key detail

Steady state ≈202 TFLOP per 12-frame chunk, about 70% of it attention against the 32,760-token cache [D]; the recipe, not the backbone, is what later world models reuse

Status and sources

NeurIPS 2025 (spotlight). Availability: code + weights. Sources: arXiv 2506.08009 Sec. 3.2-3.4, Sec. 4 (Table 1, rolling KV ablation), App. A; Self-Forcing code: wan/configs/wan_t2v_1_3B.py (30 layers, dim 1536, 12 heads, ffn 8960, patch 1x2x2); configs/self_forcing_dmd.yaml (denoising_step_list, num_frame_per_block 3, latent 21x16x60x104); pipeline/causal_inference.py (frame_seq_length 1560, timestep-0 KV refresh pass); wan/modules/causal_model.py (max_attention_size 32760, local_attn_size, sink_size); Flash-VAED arXiv 2602.19161 Table 9 (decode share).

Tencent Hunyuan and HUST · 2025 · 13B

Chunk-wise MM-DiT that re-reads its history

Causal DiTread

Details
Overview

An interactive game-video model made by full fine-tuning of the HunyuanVideo MM-DiT. Keyboard and mouse inputs are mapped to a continuous camera trajectory, turned into Plücker embeddings and added to the video tokens. It is not block-causal: each 33-frame chunk is denoised with the clean history latents concatenated into the sequence and marked by a binary mask, so history is re-processed at every step and there is no KV cache. Phased Consistency Model distillation to 8 steps lifts throughput from 0.25 to 6.6 FPS, still about 5 s per 33-frame action chunk.

Representation

HunyuanVideo causal 3D VAE latents; strides are not restated in the paper (HunyuanVideo's own report: 4x8x8, 16 channels, patch 1x2x2, which gives 3,600 tokens per latent frame at 1280x720 and ≈32,400 per 33-frame chunk of 9 latent frames [D])

Core

HunyuanVideo MM-DiT: double-stream blocks followed by single-stream blocks (Fig. 4), full-parameter fine-tuned; size not restated (13B in HunyuanVideo's report)

Attention

Bidirectional over the chunk plus the concatenated clean history latents (a single image, the last chunk or several chunks); a binary mask marks history (1) vs predicted (0) tokens; no KV cache described

Actions

W/A/S/D, arrows, Space and mouse → shared continuous camera space (translation, rotation, speed; roll removed) → Plücker embeddings → light encoder (a few conv layers + temporal pooling) → added to the video tokens after patchify with a learnable scale; token addition beat token and channel concatenation (Table 4)

Prediction

Flow matching; Phased Consistency Model distillation plus CFG distillation into an 8-step consistency model; the pre-distillation step count is not stated

Decoder

HunyuanVideo 3D VAE decoder → 33-frame chunk at 720p, 25 fps

Memory

Hybrid history condition: training mix of one history clip (0.7), several clips (0.05) and a single frame (0.25); history tokens re-enter every chunk, so cost grows with the history used; no retrieval, no 3D state

Speed

0.25 FPS undistilled → 6.6 FPS with PCM (authors, Table 2; GPU not stated); 33 frames at 6.6 FPS ≈ 5.0 s per action chunk, matching 'less than 5 s per action' [D]; trained on 192 H20 GPUs

Key detail

Control granularity is a whole 1.32 s chunk, and history is concatenated rather than cached, so every denoising step re-processes the history tokens through all layers

Status and sources

arXiv preprint. Availability: code + weights. Sources: arXiv 2506.17201 Sec. 4.1-4.3, 5.1 (implementation), Table 2, Table 4, Fig. 4-5; HunyuanVideo arXiv 2412.03603 (VAE 4x8x8x16, patch 1x2x2, 13B; not in the local corpus); GitHub Tencent-Hunyuan/Hunyuan-GameCraft-1.0 (release not re-verified in this pass).

ByteDance Seed · 2025 · 8B

Causal DiT, one adversarial pass per latent frame

Causal DiTread

Details
Overview

Autoregressive Adversarial Post-Training, the one-pass-per-frame design: a pre-trained 8B video diffusion transformer is made block-causal and post-trained adversarially so that each latent frame (4 video frames) is generated with a single network evaluation from noise, the previous generated frame recycled through channel concatenation, and a KV cache over a sliding window of 30 latent frames. Per-frame conditions (human pose, or camera rays relative to the previous frame) enter as extra input channels. The authors report 24 fps at 736x416 on one H100 with 0.16 s latency, or 1280x720 on 8 H100s, for streams up to a minute.

Representation

Causal 3D convolution VAE, 4x temporal and 8x spatial; one latent frame = 4 video frames, the first frame its own latent; DiT patch size not stated, so tokens per frame are not computed (latent grid 92x52 at 736x416 [D])

Core

8B MMDiT-style diffusion transformer with 36 blocks (base model not named); width and heads not stated; text tokens and visual tokens in one sequence; the discriminator reuses the same causal architecture (16B in training); norm and FFN details not stated

Attention

Block-causal: text tokens attend only to themselves, visual tokens to the text tokens and to visual tokens of the current and previous frames; window N = 30 latent frames (5 s) plus the text tokens and the first frame always; FlashAttention-3; 3D RoPE with a fixed temporal interval for arbitrary length

Actions

Per-frame conditions shifted to align with the frames: human pose, or camera origin and direction (CameraCtrl II style, relative to the previous frame) as new input channels with a randomly initialized input projection; the previous generated frame enters by channel concatenation

Prediction

1 NFE per latent frame: diffusion adaptation, consistency-distillation initialization, then adversarial training with student forcing (the generator rolls out with its KV cache during training; frame-wise discriminator logits, approximated R1/R2); 'one frame of compute per step' vs two for one-step diffusion forcing

Decoder

Lightweight VAE decoder: residual blocks per scale 3 → 2, channels [128, 256, 512, 512] → [64, 128, 256, 512], ≈3x faster; causal VAE allows streaming decode of 4 frames per step

Memory

Sliding window of 30 latent frames in the KV cache (constant speed and memory); the effective receptive field still grows across layers and steps, which is why training uses long student-forced rollouts

Speed

24 fps at 736x416 on one H100, 1280x720 on 8×H100, 0.16 s latency, 60 s streams of 1,440 frames (authors); 6 DiT passes per second, so ≤167 ms per latent-frame pass including decode [D]; trained on 256 H100s with 8-GPU Ulysses context parallelism

Key detail

Lowest DiT work per frame in this gallery: one pass per 4 frames (Self Forcing: 5 per 12, Matrix-Game 3.5: 3 per 12) [D]; no code or weights found

Status and sources

NeurIPS 2025. Availability: closed. Sources: arXiv 2506.09350 Sec. 1, 2.1 (causal architecture, window), 2.2 (adversarial training), 3 (VAE 4x8, N = 30), App. A (8B, 36 blocks, FlashAttention-3, RoPE, Ulysses), App. C (lightweight decoder), App. G (camera conditioning); interactive_video_dits.md (AAPT section, derived pass counts).

Stanford / Adobe · 2025 · 200M

Mamba scan plus local attention for long memory

State-spaceread

Details
Overview

An action-conditioned autoregressive video diffusion model whose backbone swaps full attention for a hybrid: a block-wise Mamba scan carries long-term memory across frames in a fixed-size state, and frame-local attention keeps nearby frames sharp. Trained with diffusion forcing (independent per-frame noise) plus a clean-prefix scheme that forces the model to use distant context. Per-frame inference cost and memory stay constant with rollout length, unlike a growing KV cache.

Representation

VAE latents per frame: an internal spatio-temporal VAE on Memory Maze, the DFoT image VAE on Minecraft; tokens scanned spatial-major, time-minor; resolution not stated ('low-resolution synthetic videos')

Core

CogVideoX-style diffusion blocks (AdaLN, FFN) with the attention block replaced by a block-wise SSM scan followed by frame-local attention; 200M parameters (all compared models matched at 200M by adjusting the layer count); layers and width not disclosed

Attention

Frame-local attention: bidirectional within a 5-frame chunk, causal to the previous chunk, effective window k = 10 frames (FlexAttention). The SSM scans over time independently per spatial block (b_h, b_w), block sizes differing by layer to trade spatial coherence for temporal memory

Actions

Continuous actions (camera position) through a small MLP added to the noise-level embedding, injected by adaptive normalisation; discrete Minecraft actions as learned embeddings

Prediction

Diffusion forcing: one frame per autoregressive step, denoised conditioned on clean past frames; training keeps a random clean prefix (p = 0.5, longer than half the sequence); number of denoising steps not disclosed

Decoder

VAE decoder of the respective latent space (not described further)

Memory

Per layer: a KV cache for the last k frames plus one fixed-size SSM state per block, so memory and per-frame time are constant in rollout length (Table 1: linear training, constant per-frame inference, long memory); recalls content from 400+ frames back

Speed

No numbers in the text: Fig. 8 plots training time per iteration vs 200-800 training frames and inference memory and time per frame vs frames generated (flat for this model, growing for causal attention); hardware not stated

Key detail

Trained on 400-frame videos, then fine-tuned on 800; FVD 38.9 on 560 frames after 240 context vs 45.1 for a full-context causal transformer and 163 for plain Mamba2 (authors, Table S1)

Status and sources

arXiv preprint. Availability: closed. Sources: arXiv 2505.20171 Sec. 3-4 (architecture, block-wise scan, frame-local attention, action condition, fixed-length state), Table 1; arXiv 2505.20171 Sec. 5.1 (datasets), Sec. 5.3 and Fig. 8 (costs), Supp. S1 Table S1 (FVD); arXiv 2505.20171 Supp. S2 (VAEs, CogVideoX-style blocks, 200M, k = 10, chunks of 5, training schedule).

University of Washington, TRI · 2025 · ~85M + ResNet-18

Two timesteps turn one DiT into policy or dynamics

World-actionread

Details
Overview

A small diffusion transformer that couples an action diffusion process and a future-image diffusion process with two independent timesteps. Fixing a timestep at T marginalises that modality and fixing it at 0 conditions on it, so one network is a policy, a forward model, an inverse model or a video predictor. The current frames condition every block through AdaLN (ResNet-18 features), while the future frames are SDXL-VAE latents patchified into tokens next to 16 action tokens and 8 registers.

Representation

Future observation: 224x224 frames → frozen SDXL VAE → 28x28x4 latents, patchified (4,4,2) → 49 tokens per camera per 2-frame stack [D]; current observation (h_o = 2 frames per camera) → trainable ImageNet-initialised ResNet-18 features, used only as AdaLN conditioning

Core

DiT with AdaLN: depth 12, d 768, 12 heads, MLP ratio 4, 8 register tokens; ~85M in the blocks [D: 12 x 12 x 768^2]; trained from scratch, no base video model; MLP activation not stated

Attention

Bidirectional over action tokens + future-image patches + registers; for the 3-camera DROID setup 16 + 3 x 49 + 8 = 171 tokens [D]; learnable positional embedding

Actions

16-step action chunk, one token per step through a shallow shared MLP; AdaLN carries the two timestep embeddings (action, image) and the ResNet features; 8 actions executed before replanning

Prediction

DDPM training with 100 steps, DDIM sampling with 10; policy mode fixes the image timestep at T, so the image tokens are pure noise but stay in the sequence

Decoder

SDXL VAE decoder, only when images are sampled (forward dynamics, video); the policy never decodes

Memory

None beyond the 2-frame observation stack

Speed

Inference latency not disclosed; the robot runs at 10 Hz with delta end-effector actions; DROID pretraining of 100K steps takes 24 h on 4 A100 (authors)

Key detail

Per chunk ~10 passes of an 85M-parameter block stack over ~171 tokens ≈ 0.3 TFLOP [D]; about 165x fewer backbone parameters than DreamZero [D]

Status and sources

RSS 2025. Availability: code. Sources: arXiv 2504.02792 Sec. III-B/C (coupled timesteps, architecture, registers), App. A (implementation, DDIM, 24 h on 4 A100), App. C (10 Hz control), Table V (hyperparameters).

Microsoft Research · 2025 · 1.2B

Minecraft GPT, decoded along anti-diagonals

Token videoread

Details
Overview

An open, real-time Minecraft world model: a LLaMA-style decoder trained from scratch on interleaved frame and action tokens. A VQ-VAE with 16x compression turns each 224x384 frame into 336 tokens (14x24, codebook 8,192) and each action into 11 tokens. Diagonal decoding releases tokens along anti-diagonals, cutting the 336 dependent steps per frame to 37, and a fine-tune with a matching attention mask recovers the quality; the 1.2B model goes from 0.89 to 3.01 FPS.

Representation

336 discrete tokens per 224x384 frame (14x24 from a VQ-VAE with 16x spatial compression, codebook 8,192); frames downscaled from 360x640 'to reduce the computation'

Core

LLaMA architecture (RMSNorm, rotary embeddings): 1.2B = 20 layers, d 2048, MLP 8192, 32 heads; 700M = 20 layers, d 2048, MLP 4096; 300M = 20 layers, d 1024, 16 heads; activation not disclosed

Attention

Dense causal over 16-frame clips: 16 x 347 = 5,552 tokens [D]; vocabulary 8,192 + 70 = 8,262

Actions

11 action tokens per step ([aBOS], 9 action tokens incl. 2 camera tokens, [aEOS]) interleaved after each frame; the model predicts actions too, so it doubles as a policy

Prediction

Next-token AR, or diagonal decoding: tokens (i, j+1) and (i+1, j) are released together, 37 passes per frame instead of 336 (theoretical 9.1x) [D]; fine-tuned with a matching parallel attention mask

Decoder

VQ-VAE decoder → 224x384 frame

Memory

KV policy not disclosed; 16-frame context

Speed

1.2B: 0.89 FPS autoregressive, 3.01 FPS with diagonal decoding; 300M: 2.00 / 5.91 FPS (authors, Table 2; inference GPU not stated). Trained on 32 A100-40GB for 200k steps

Key detail

9.1x fewer dependent passes buys 3.4x in FPS [D]: each diagonal step of up to 14 tokens is still latency-bound; the authors' real-time bar is 2 FPS for amateurs and 5 FPS for professionals

Status and sources

arXiv preprint. Availability: code + weights. Sources: arXiv 2504.08388 Sec. 2.1-2.3 (tokenizer, decoder, diagonal decoding), Sec. 3.1-3.2 (data, training), Tables 1-2, App. B Table 6; verified_findings Finding 10 (MineWorld speed figures as cited by Dreamer 4).

University of Würzburg · 2025 · ~8-9M transformer

DreamerV3 with a transformer and contrastive loss

RL world modelverified

Details
Overview

DreamerV3 with its GRU replaced by a small Transformer State-Space Model and an extra action-conditioned contrastive objective. A CNN VAE encodes 64x64 frames as 32x32 categoricals, an action mixer fuses state and action into one token, and a 4-block causal transformer with Transformer-XL relative positions predicts the next state, reward and continuation. The cache is capped at 8 steps, so per-step memory is bounded. The score gain comes from AC-CPC, which predicts features 10 steps ahead given the future actions, not from the transformer swap.

Representation

32 categoricals x 32 classes per 64x64 RGB frame from a CNN VAE (4 strided conv layers)

Core

TSSM: 4 blocks, d 512, 8 heads, FFN 1024, dropout 0.1; ~8-9M transformer parameters (repo preset estimate)

Attention

Causal self-attention with Transformer-XL relative positions; attention context 8 steps; training sequences T = 64, batch 16

Actions

Action mixer (Linear + LN + SiLU to 512) fuses the flattened 32x32 state with the one-hot action into one token

Prediction

One pass per imagined step; a dynamics-predictor MLP samples the next categorical state from h_t; imagination horizon 15

Decoder

CNN decoder reconstructs from z_t for training only; the actor-critic uses s_t = {h_t, z_t}, so nothing is decoded in imagination

Memory

Hidden states of the previous segment are cached and reused as context; the released code caps the cache at 8 steps (att_context_left = 8)

Speed

No inference or wall-clock figure in the paper; Atari 100k mean/median HNS 162/77 (authors)

Key detail

AC-CPC: InfoNCE prediction of latent features K = 10 steps (~0.67 s) ahead, conditioned on future actions; without the action conditioning HNS drops from 162/77 to 111/42

Status and sources

ICLR 2025. Availability: code. Sources: verified_findings Finding 5 (arXiv 2503.04416 Tables 4, 6, 7, 9; github.com/burchim/TWISTER att_context_left = 8); arXiv 2503.04416 Sec. 3.1-3.2, App. A.3 Table 9.

Factorized-attention DiT over five cameras

Driving & robotsread

Details
Overview

Wayve's multi-camera driving world model: a video tokenizer with 32x spatial and 8x temporal compression turns 5 camera streams into 64-channel latents, and an 8.4B space-time factorized transformer denoises them with flow matching, conditioned on the ego action through adaptive LayerNorm and on agents, maps and scene metadata through cross-attention. It runs 50 denoising steps with no distillation and no KV cache; Wayve reports no inference speed and calls real-time synthesis future work.

Representation

Video tokenizer (space-time factorized transformer, 85M encoder / 200M decoder): 8x temporal, 32x spatial, 64 channels; 24 frames at 448x960 → 3x14x30 latents (≈400x compression); 420 latents per camera per latent step, 2,100 across 5 cameras [D]

Core

22 space-time factorized transformer blocks, d 4096, 32 heads; each block: spatial attention (over space and cameras), temporal attention, cross-attention, MLP with adaptive LayerNorm; QK-norm; 8.4B parameters trained from scratch

Attention

Factorized: spatial attention over 2,100 tokens (5 cameras × 420), temporal attention over 6 latent steps; training window 48 frames × 5 cameras = 12,600 tokens; no full 3D attention; sinusoidal space and timestamp encodings plus learned camera geometry, re-added at the start of every block

Actions

Ego-vehicle action and flow-matching time via adaptive LayerNorm in every block (found more accurate than cross-attention); agents, metadata, camera parameters and external embeddings via cross-attention

Prediction

Flow matching, 50 denoising steps, linear-quadratic schedule, no distillation; CFG off by default (scale 2-20 for hard cases); rollout: k=3 context latents, predict the next latents, append, slide the window

Decoder

200M transformer decoder with full spatiotemporal attention: 3 latent steps → 24 frames at 448x960 per camera, decoded with a sliding window

Memory

Sliding window of latents; no KV cache described

Speed

Not disclosed; 'real-time or near-real-time video synthesis remains computationally intensive', distillation listed as future work (authors); ≈1.1e16 dense FLOPs per 50-step, 48-frame, 5-camera window [D]

Key detail

Wayve chose 32x spatial / 64-channel latents because shorter sequences give faster inference; an offline simulator where throughput, not latency, matters; ≈1.5e12 training tokens on 256 H100s [D]

Status and sources

company technical report (arXiv 2503.20523). Availability: closed. Sources: GAIA-2 report (local src/gaia2.txt): Sec. 2.1.1 tokenizer, 2.2 world model (22 blocks, C=4096, 32 heads, adaptive LayerNorm), 3 training (12,600 tokens, 128/256 H100), 4 inference (50 steps, k=3, CFG), 8 future work; ar_token_and_physical_ai.md Group 2 (derived counts).

Stanford · 2025 · not disclosed

Video and action heads on one masked transformer

World-actionread

Details
Overview

A masked-autoencoder-style transformer, initialised from MAR-B, that fuses a history of kl-f16 VAE latents and action chunks into a joint video-action latent, which two lightweight diffusion heads decode into video patches and actions. Denoising runs only in the small heads, never in the backbone, and at deployment the video head is skipped entirely, so a 16-action trajectory costs 95 ms on an RTX 3080: 40 ms of VAE encoding, 40 ms of transformer (30 with flash attention) and 15 ms for 16 steps of the action head.

Representation

Pretrained kl-f16 VAE latent map (w x h x c) per frame, flattened and projected by an FC layer into N tokens of width d; N and the input resolution are not stated; future frames enter as randomly masked tokens concatenated channel-wise with the history tokens

Core

Bidirectional transformer initialised from MAR-B (MAR-B as released: 12 encoder + 12 decoder blocks, d 768, 12 heads, per the MAR code); UVA's own size is not stated; language as a CLIP text token repeated M times plus cross-attention (Libero10); block details not disclosed

Attention

Bidirectional over the N x h video-action tokens (+ M language tokens); the same positions are masked in every frame to avoid leakage; attention is about half of the transformer time (40 → 30 ms with flash attention)

Actions

Each frame pairs with a chunk of L actions sampled faster than frames; history chunks are repeated M times, FC-projected to N action tokens and concatenated channel-wise with the visual tokens

Prediction

Video: MAR-style masked generation from an empty sequence in 1 to 8 autoregressive stages; actions: a conv + MLP pool the N latents into one action latent that conditions the action diffusion head, 16 denoising steps on the robot (100 in simulation)

Decoder

Video diffusion head + VAE decoder exist but are skipped at deployment (100 ms at 16 steps, 625 ms at 100)

Memory

History window of h frames and action chunks; no KV cache

Speed

Per 16-action trajectory on an RTX 3080 (authors, Table VI): VAE encoder 40 ms, transformer 40 ms (30 with flash attention), action head 15 ms at 16 steps (93 at 100); total 95 ms (85 with flash attention), 173 ms at 100 steps; policy + planner 195 ms; simulation timings on L40

Key detail

The clearest train-with-video, deploy-without-it case: the skipped video head would cost more than the whole 95 ms policy, and the VAE encoder plus backbone, not the action head, dominate (80 of 95 ms [D])

Status and sources

arXiv preprint (v3 Apr 2025). Availability: code + weights. Sources: arXiv 2503.00200 Sec. III-A/B/C (encoding, masked transformer, diffusion heads), V-D (16 vs 100 steps, attention share), App. X-A (autoregressive video stages), X-D and Table VI (timing); GitHub README (MAR + VAE initialisation, checkpoints, 8 H100 x 4 days); GitHub LTH14/mar models/mar.py (mar_base: 12 + 12 blocks, d 768, 12 heads; fetched).

NVIDIA's autoregressive world foundation models: Llama3-style GPTs trained from scratch to predict the next video token, with no language pretraining.
