company technical report. Availability: code + weights. Sources: Cosmos technical report arXiv 2501.03575 Sec. 4 (tokenizer), Sec. 5.2.2-5.2.4 (architecture table, Medusa, Tables 15-17), post-training section (ActionCond); ar_token notes Group 1 (Cosmos-Predict1 AR) for the [D] arithmetic.

arXiv · code · SVG

Meta FAIR · 2024 · 1B

Navigation DiT that cross-attends to past frames

Driving & robotsread

Details
Overview

A navigation world model for robots that predicts the next egocentric frame latent from past frames and a 3-DoF navigation action. Its Conditional Diffusion Transformer runs self-attention only over the tokens of the frame being denoised and reads the 4 context frames through cross-attention, so cost is linear in the context length (about 4x fewer FLOPs than a DiT over all frames). Planning is model-predictive control with the cross-entropy method, or ranking 32 trajectories from an external policy. The default 250 denoising steps make a 4 s trajectory cost 30.3 s on an RTX 6000 Ada; distillation to 6 steps and time skipping bring it to 0.4 s (authors).

Representation

Stable Diffusion VAE latents, 'similar as in DiT'; input resolution and tokens per frame are not stated in the paper text read; rollouts at 4 FPS

Core

CDiT-XL, 1B parameters (sizes S to XL); depth, width and heads not stated in the text read; block = self-attention over the target frame, cross-attention to context frames with a skip connection, MLP; AdaLN scale, shift and gates

Attention

Self-attention within the target frame only (n tokens); cross-attention from target queries to the tokens of m = 4 context frames as keys and values; cost O(m n² d) vs O(m² n² d) for a full DiT; CDiT-L is 4x faster than DiT-XL at equal parameters with better prediction

Actions

Navigation action a = (u ∈ R² translation, yaw φ) plus time shift k (up to ±16 s) and diffusion timestep t: each scalar → sine-cosine features → 2-layer MLP, summed into one vector that drives AdaLN; actions omitted for unlabeled Ego4D training

Prediction

DDPM with the DiT noise schedule and learned covariance (VLB loss); 250 denoising steps by default, distilled to 6 (FastVideo DiT distillation); 'Time Skip' composes adjacent action pairs to simulate 8 instead of 16 states for 4 s

Decoder

SD VAE decoder → pixels, used for LPIPS goal scoring during planning and for visualization

Memory

4 context frames re-encoded as cross-attention keys and values at every step; no KV cache discussed; loses context on out-of-distribution data (mode collapse noted by the authors)

Speed

One 4 s trajectory (16 states) on one RTX 6000 Ada: 30.3 s default → 14.7 s with Time Skip (8 states) → 0.4 s with 6-step distillation → 0.1 s with 4-bit quantization (estimated, not measured) (authors, Table 8); ≈7-8 ms per 1B pass in every configuration [D]; trained on 64 H100s

Key detail

All of the 75x speedup comes from fewer passes (250 → 6 steps, 16 → 8 states), none from cheaper passes; planning evaluates 32 independent trajectories, 8 states × 6 steps = 1,536 batchable passes per decision [D]

Status and sources

CVPR 2025. Availability: code + weights. Sources: NWM paper page (local src/nwm.txt): Sec. 3.1-3.3 (CDiT block, action encoding, AdaLN, complexity), 4 (implementation: CDiT-XL 1B, 4 context frames, SD VAE, 64 H100), 4.4 (planning), App. 7 and Table 8 (runtime); ar_token_and_physical_ai.md Group 2 (derived per-pass time); code link from the project page (release not re-verified in this pass).

Embedding predictorread

Details
Overview

A task-agnostic latent world model that predicts future DINOv2 patch features instead of pixels. A frozen DINOv2 turns each 196x196 frame into 196 patch features of width 384, and a small ViT predictor (6 layers, ~19M parameters) regresses the next frame's features from a history of 3 frames, with the action and proprioception embeddings concatenated onto every patch vector rather than added as tokens. Goals are images; planning is cross-entropy-method search in feature space, and the pixel decoder exists only for visualization.

Representation

196 patch features (14x14 x 384) per frame resized to 196x196, from a frozen DINOv2 encoder (variant not named in the paper; 384-d is the ViT-S/14 size [D])

Core

ViT with the patch-embedding layer removed, used as a decoder-only predictor: depth 6, 16 heads, MLP 2048, ~19M parameters; token width = 384 features + 10-d action embedding (+ 10-d proprio) [D]; positional encoding not disclosed

Attention

Frame-level causal mask: every patch of frame t attends to all patches of frames t-H..t-1 (no token-level autoregression); H = 3 (PointMaze, Reacher, Push-T, PushObj) or 1 (Wall, Rope, Granular); at most 3 x 196 = 588 tokens [D]

Actions

An MLP maps the action to a 10-d embedding that is concatenated to every patch vector (channels, not tokens); proprioception enters the same way; frameskip 5 (1 for Rope and Granular)

Prediction

One pass regresses the next frame's 196 features (MSE in latent space); no sampling, no pixels

Decoder

Optional transposed-convolution decoder trained separately, for visualization only; training the predictor through its loss lowers Push-T success (0.92 → 0.80)

Memory

Fixed window of H frames; no KV cache or long-term memory

Speed

One predictor step at batch 32: 0.014 s; a full CEM plan (100 samples x 10 iterations): 53.0 s, both on one A6000 (authors); LeWM later measured 47 s per DINO-WM plan (hardware not stated)

Key detail

196 tokens per frame make every CEM sample a 588-token ViT pass; LeWM's one-token-per-frame design runs the same kind of plan in ~1 s

Status and sources

ICML 2025. Availability: code + weights. Sources: arXiv 2411.04983 Sec. 3.1 (encoder, predictor, decoder, planning), App. A.4.2-A.4.3, A.5.1, Table 10 (timing), A.9 and Tables 11-12 (hyperparameters); GitHub gaoyuezhou/dino_wm conf/predictor/vit.yaml (depth 6, heads 16, mlp_dim 2048) and conf/train.yaml (action and proprio emb dim 10, num_hist 3, frameskip 5); fetched, no explicit width; LeWM arXiv 2603.19312 Fig. 3 (47 s DINO-WM plan).

University of Bonn · 2024 · 12M

Dreamer-style RL that imagines in object slots

Object-centricread

Details
Overview

Dreamer-style model-based RL on object slots instead of one holistic latent. A SAVi encoder (pretrained, then fine-tuned) turns each frame into 2-10 slots of 128-d; an OCVP-style dynamics transformer predicts the next slot set from the slot history and the actions; a second Slot Aggregation Transformer with per-step output tokens drives the reward, value and actor heads, and the actor-critic trains on 15-step imagined slot rollouts. Two 4-layer transformers run per imagined step, with cost set by the slot count rather than the image resolution.

Representation

N = 2-10 object slots of 128-d per frame from SAVi (learned slot init, 3 Slot Attention iterations on the first frame, 1 afterwards); slots projected to 256-d tokens; frame size not stated in the text

Core

Dynamics: OCVP-Seq transformer encoder, 4 layers, d 256, 8 heads, FFN 512. Slot Aggregation Transformer (SAT) for reward, value and actor: 4 causal layers, d 256, 8 heads, FFN 512, RMSNorm; 12M parameters in total; dynamics norm and activation not disclosed

Attention

Dynamics: OCVP sequential pattern, temporal attention (each slot over its own history) then relational attention (all slots of one step). SAT: causal over time with ALiBi recency bias; 1 [out] + 4 [reg] tokens per step, which cannot attend to earlier [out]/[reg] tokens

Actions

4-D end-effector + gripper commands a_0:t are inputs to the dynamics transformer alongside the slot history (the embedding mechanism is not spelled out in the paper)

Prediction

One pass predicts all N next slots (regression): joint-embedding loss to SAVi slots of the real next frame plus image reconstruction through the SAVi decoder; no teacher forcing; S seed frames then T = 15 imagined steps

Decoder

SAVi CNN spatial-broadcast decoder: per-slot RGB + alpha masks composited by weighted sum; used in the dynamics loss and for visualisation, not by the actor

Memory

The dynamics model and SAT re-read the slot history each step (S + imagined steps); no KV cache mentioned

Speed

No inference or wall-clock figure; everything trains on one A100 40 GB (authors)

Key detail

Reward, value and actor are MLP heads on SAT [out] tokens, with symlog two-hot reward/value bins as in DreamerV3; per-step cost scales with the number of slots N, not with pixels; the actor head outputs a Gaussian (μ, σ)

Status and sources

arXiv preprint (v2 Feb 2025). Availability: code. Sources: arXiv 2410.08822 Sec. 2 (SAVi, OCVP), Sec. 3.1-3.2 (dynamics, SAT, rewards, imagination), Eq. 3-11; arXiv 2410.08822 App. D Table 2 and D.1-D.4 (SAVi, dynamics, SAT configs; 12M params; one A100 40 GB; horizon 15, λ 0.95); arXiv 2410.08822 App. F (4-D action vector).

Decart and Etched · 2024 · 500M

Open per-frame Minecraft DiT, space-time attention

Causal DiTread

Details
Overview

An early playable real-time diffusion world model (Minecraft), released with open 500M weights. A ViT autoencoder maps each 360x640 frame to 144 latent tokens, and a small DiT generates one frame at a time with full spatial attention inside the frame and causal temporal attention over a 32-frame window, trained with Diffusion Forcing. Each pass carries only 144 tokens, so batch-1 serving is bound by weight reads rather than by FLOPs; Decart's custom kernels and multi-GPU engine behind the 20 fps demo are closed.

Representation

ViT-L/20 KL-VAE: 360x640 frame → 18x32 latent with 16 channels, no temporal compression; DiT patch 2 → 144 tokens per frame [D]

Core

DiT-S/2 (open-oasis): 16 blocks, d 1024, 16 heads, MLP ratio 4; each block = spatial attention + MLP, then temporal attention + MLP, each pair with its own adaLN; no pretrained video base named

Attention

Factorized: full (bidirectional) spatial attention over the 144 tokens of a frame; causal temporal axial attention per spatial position over up to 32 frames; axial RoPE in space, RoPE in time

Actions

25-dim one-hot keyboard and mouse vector per frame → Linear(25, 1024), added to the timestep embedding that drives the adaLN modulations

Prediction

Diffusion Forcing (independent noise level per frame), v-prediction, sigmoid beta schedule; reference sampler DDIM with 10 steps per frame, context frames held at noise level 14; the demo's step count is not disclosed

Decoder

ViT-L/20 decoder (12 layers, width 1024) → 360x640 frame, once per generated frame

Memory

Sliding window of 32 frames; no KV cache in the reference loop, so every DDIM step re-runs the whole window (up to 32 × 144 = 4,608 tokens [D]); blog lists limited long-horizon memory as a known failure

Speed

360p at 20 fps, 47 ms per frame, on NVIDIA H100s (company claim; GPUs per stream and demo checkpoint size not disclosed); the open 500M model runs at 2.58 FPS in MineWorld's Table 1 (third party, GPU not stated)

Key detail

Per-frame generation with 144-token passes: ≈0.12 TFLOP per cached pass against ≈1 GB of BF16 weights, so single-stream decoding is weight-bandwidth-bound and batching users is the lever [D]

Status and sources

blog post (web technical report). Availability: code + weights. Sources: open-oasis dit.py (DiT_S_2: hidden 1024, depth 16, 16 heads; external_cond Linear(25, 1024); max_frames 32); open-oasis attention.py (spatial is_causal=False, temporal is_causal=True); open-oasis vae.py (ViT-L/20: patch 20, enc 6 / dec 12 layers, width 1024, latent 16); open-oasis generate.py (DDIM 10 steps, stabilization level 15, 20 fps output); oasis-model.github.io (Diffusion Forcing, 500M weights, 20 fps); Decart release article (47 ms per frame on H100s, custom kernels); MineWorld arXiv 2504.08388 Table 1 (Oasis 500M at 2.58 FPS).

CASIA / Alibaba · 2024 · 150M

One GPT for Atari dynamics and Q-values

RL world modelread

Details
Overview

An offline, multi-game world-action model: one GPT-2-style transformer over IRIS-like token sequences learns the world model (next observation tokens, reward, termination) and the Q-function at the same time, pretrained on 15 Atari games with 10M transitions each. At decision time a short beam search (horizon 2) over the model's own imagined futures corrects the Q-estimates. Beams are batched, but every imagined frame still costs 36 sequential token decodes, and planning drops throughput from 10.8 to 1.26 FPS.

Representation

VQ-VAE on 84×84 grayscale frames: 36 tokens per frame (6×6 [D]), vocabulary 2048; 3-layer CNN with self-attention at resolutions 6 and 12 (IRIS code base), frozen after stage 1

Core

GPT-2 (minGPT): JOWA-150M 12 layers, hidden 768, 12 heads; JOWA-70M 6 × 768 × 12; JOWA-40M 4 × 512 × 8; dropout 0.1; input = vocabulary + position + learnable task embedding

Attention

Causal over interleaved (z_t^1..z_t^36, a_t) tokens; L = 8 steps, max 296 tokens (8 × 37 [D])

Actions

One action token per step (18-action Atari space) plus a task embedding; the Q-head reads the transformer output at the observation tokens; next-code, reward and done heads are 2-layer MLPs, the Q-head a 3-layer MLP (hidden 1,792, 3 distributional heads) trained by TD with CQL

Prediction

Next observation token autoregressive within a frame, z_t^k | z_≤t-1, z_t^<k, a_≤t-1, so 36 serial decodes per imagined frame [D]; reward sign {-1, 0, 1} and termination as classification; distributional Q-head (3-layer MLP, hidden 1792, 3 heads for 150M) trained by TD learning

Decoder

VQ-VAE CNN decoder for reconstruction only; planning and Q-values stay in token space

Memory

Context of 8 steps = 296 tokens; no KV-cache details given

Speed

JOWA-150M on 7 games: 10.8 FPS without planning, 1.26 FPS with beam search (H = 2, K = 2-4), 0.12 FPS with MCTS; hardware not stated (authors, Table 5). Pretraining 1.75M steps, 'around 12 days on A100 GPUs', GPU count not given

Key detail

Beam search calls the world model K²(H−1)+K times but takes only H forward latencies because beams are batched; at H = 2 that is still ~72 serial token decodes per action [D], ~0.8 s at 1.26 FPS [D]

Status and sources

ICLR 2025. Availability: code + weights. Sources: arXiv 2410.00564 Sec. 3 (84×84, 18 actions), Sec. 4.1-4.2 (architecture, Eq. 4-6, beam search cost), Sec. 5 (K = 36, L = 8, H = 2); arXiv 2410.00564 Table 5 (FPS), Tables 9-12 (VQ-VAE, transformer, Q-head configs), Table 17 (beam widths), Sec. 3 (12 A100-days).

Details
Overview

IRIS with context-aware tokens. A CNN autoencoder conditioned on the previous frame and action encodes only the stochastic change between steps as 4 delta tokens from a 1,024-entry vocabulary, and a 3-layer GPT sees 6 tokens per step instead of IRIS's 17: one continuous I-token (a frame embedding from an auxiliary CNN), one action token and the 4 delta tokens. 4 delta tokens per 64x64 frame, vocabulary 1,024, from a CNN autoencoder conditioned on the previous frame and action; plus 1 continuous I-token per step from an auxiliary CNN

Core

GPT-like causal transformer: 3 layers, d 512, 8 heads; 25M parameters for the whole agent (Table 1); block details not disclosed

Attention

Causal over 6 tokens per step (I-token, action, 4 deltas); context 21 timesteps = 126 tokens [D]

Actions

One action token per step from a learned embedding table

Prediction

Next delta token by softmax over 1,024 codes: 4 dependent passes per frame; reward and termination come from the action-token position

Decoder

CNN decoder conditioned on the previous frame, action and delta tokens runs every imagined step: the CNN+LSTM policy sees decoded frames and the next I-token is computed from them

Full causal context of 21 steps; cache handling not restated beyond IRIS

20 environment frames per second of training on one A100 40GB in Crafter, vs 2 for IRIS-64, 6 for IRIS-16, 30-40 for DreamerV3 (authors); 12 FPS on an RTX 3090 (measured by EMERALD); Atari 100k in 26 h, 5x IRIS

6 tokens per step instead of 17, not fewer passes: 4 serial token decodes plus a decoder call per frame, because the I-token comes from the decoded frame

Overview

A GPT world model for robot manipulation with a compressive tokenizer: context frames are encoded on their own into 16x16 = 256 VQ tokens, but every future frame is encoded, conditioned on the context frames through cross-attention, into only 4x4 = 16 tokens. Compressive conditional VQGAN (114M at 64x64): 256 tokens per context frame, 16 tokens per future frame, codebooks of 8,192 each; transformer vocabulary 16,386 incl. 2 slot tokens

Core

LLaMA-style GPT (RMSNorm, SwiGLU, RoPE): 12 layers, d 768, 12 heads, FFN 3072, 138M; scaling run 24 layers, d 1024, 16 heads, 436M

Attention

Dense causal over the interleaved clip: L = (N+1) T0 + (n+1)(T - T0) - 1 = 751 tokens for 16 frames with 2 context frames [D]

Actions

Action linearly projected and added to the slot-token embedding before each future frame; optional reward head on the last token of each frame (MSE)

Prediction

Next-token softmax with top-k 100: 17 passes per future frame (slot + 16 tokens) against 257 with a per-frame 16x16 tokenizer [D]

Conditional VQGAN decoder with cross-attention to the context-frame features → 64x64 (a 256x256 variant uses a 310M VQGAN)

Memory

KV policy not disclosed; the whole 12-16-frame clip stays in context

RTX 4090, batch 1: tokenize 0.29 s, generation 1.11 s, detokenize 0.06 s, 2.33 GB; 22.5 s generation with a 16x16-per-frame tokenizer (authors, Table 8; rollout length not stated in the caption)

RetNet over VQ codes, a whole frame at a time

RL world modelread

Details
Overview

An IRIS-style token world model whose transformer is replaced by a Retentive Network and whose per-token decode loop is removed. Retention keeps a fixed-size recurrent state instead of a KV cache, and Parallel Observation Prediction (POP) feeds 64 learned prediction tokens from that state to sample all 64 next-frame codes in one call. Imagination becomes 2 calls per frame instead of 64, which the authors measure as 15.4× faster than prior token-based world models.

Representation

64 VQ codes per 64×64 frame (8×8 grid), vocabulary 512; VQ-GAN-style CNN tokenizer without the discriminator (IRIS uses 16 codes)

Core

RetNet (retention, not softmax attention): 5 layers, 4 retention heads, d 256, FFN 1024, dropout 0.1; parameter count not disclosed (~3.9M block weights [D]); FFN activation not disclosed

Attention

Multi-scale retention with a per-head exponential decay and relative position; chunkwise mode is parallel inside a chunk of c = 3 observation-action blocks (195 tokens [D]) and recurrent between chunks through a d×d state per head; world-model context 2 frames

Actions

One action token per step (learned embedding) after the 64 observation tokens; reward and termination are read from the action token; the world model reuses the tokenizer's embedding table

Prediction

POP: K = 64 learned prediction tokens u are run from the recurrent state S_t and all next-frame tokens are sampled in one pass; default mode = 2 sequential calls per imagined frame (state update with z_t, a_t, then prediction with u), so 2H calls over the horizon H = 10 instead of KH = 640 (Table 6)

Decoder

VQ-VAE CNN decoder for the reconstruction loss only; the actor-critic reads the token code vectors through a small CNN + LSTM, so imagination decodes no pixels

Memory

Fixed-size retention state per layer and head replaces a growing KV cache; u tokens never enter the state update

Speed

15.4× faster imagination than prior token-based world models and under 12 h of training per game (authors); run times measured on an RTX 4090 workstation, other experiments on V100s

Key detail

POP doubles the tokens per observation prediction (2K vs K, Table 6) but turns KH sequential calls into 2H; superhuman on 12 of 26 Atari 100k games (authors)

Status and sources

ICML 2024. Availability: code. Sources: arXiv 2402.05643 Sec. 2.2-2.4 (retention, POP, training), Fig. 4, Sec. 4 (K = 64, RTX 4090 / V100), abstract (15.4×, < 12 h); arXiv 2402.05643 Table 2 (H 10, N 512, 64×64), Table 5 (world-model config), Table 6 (call counts), Table 8 and A.1.3 (actor-critic input).

NeurIPS 2023. Availability: code. Sources: verified_findings Finding 3 (arXiv 2310.09615 Tables 1, 5-10, 12; github.com/weipu-zhang/STORM); arXiv 2310.09615 Sec. 3.1-3.2 (action mixer, KV cache, agent state [z_t, h_t]).

arXiv · code · SVG

Wayve · 2023 · 6.5B

Driving video tokens, decoded one at a time

Token videoread

Details
Overview

A generative world model for driving: a 6.5B causal transformer predicts the next image token over an interleaved sequence of text, image and action tokens, trained from scratch on 4,700 h of London driving. Each 288x512 frame is 576 discrete tokens from a 0.3B DINO-distilled tokenizer, so one frame costs 576 serial passes, and a separate 2.6B video diffusion U-Net, not a transformer, turns the tokens into pixels with 50 DDIM steps. The report says the model does not yet run in real time.

Representation

576 discrete tokens per 288x512 frame (18x32, downsampling 16), vocabulary 8,192, from a 0.3B image tokenizer trained with a DINO distillation loss

Core

6.5B decoder-only transformer trained from scratch; layer, width and head counts not disclosed

Attention

Dense causal attention over 26 frames at 6.25 Hz (4 s): 26 x (32 text + 576 image + 2 action) = 15,860 tokens; FlashAttention v2; sliding window beyond the context

Actions

2 action tokens and 32 T5-large text tokens per step in the interleaved sequence; conditioning tokens are dropped at random in training, giving unconditional, action- and text-conditioned generation

Prediction

Next-token softmax with top-k = 50: 'n forward steps to generate one new image frame', so 576 serial passes per frame; optional classifier-free guidance doubles the evaluations [D]

Decoder

2.6B video diffusion 3D U-Net with factorized space/time attention: 50 DDIM steps per window of 7 frames (2 overlapping context frames), then temporal upsampling 6.25 → 12.5 → 25 Hz

Memory

KV-cache policy not disclosed; context capped at 26 frames with a sliding window for longer rollouts

Speed

Not disclosed; generation 'does not yet run at real-time' (authors). Training: world model 15 days on 64 A100-80GB, tokenizer 4 days on 32, decoder 15 days on 32 = ~1,568 A100-days [D]

Key detail

576 dependent decode steps per frame through 6.5B parameters, at least 13 GB of bf16 weights streamed per step [D], followed by a 50-step diffusion decoder: a bandwidth-bound workload

Status and sources

company technical report. Availability: closed. Sources: arXiv 2309.17080 Sec. 2.1-2.4 (tokens, world model, decoder), Sec. 4.1-4.3 (sizes, training), Sec. 5.1-5.2 (sampling, DDIM), Sec. 8 (not real time); ar_token notes Group 1 (GAIA-1) for the [D] arithmetic.

arXiv · SVG

UC San Diego · 2023 · 33B

Frozen LLM as world model inside tree search

LLM & coderead

Details
Overview

The template for using an off-the-shelf LLM as a world model. A frozen LLaMA-33B is prompted three ways: as the policy that proposes actions, as the world model that writes the next state in natural language, and as the reward model. Monte Carlo tree search runs 10-20 iterations over these text states before one answer is committed. Every tree expansion is a full LLM generation, so inference is serial 33B decoding inside a search loop, with no training at all.

Representation

A state is natural-language text: the block configuration (Blocksworld), the values of intermediate variables (GSM8k) or the current fact (PrOntoQA); an action is a text step (a block move, a sub-question, a rule)

Core

LLaMA-33B used frozen with prompts (60 layers, d 6656, 52 heads, 32.5B; LLaMA paper Table 2); the same model serves as policy, world model and reward model; Llama-2 70B in the full-Blocksworld experiment

Attention

Ordinary causal LLM attention over prompt (in-context demonstrations + state) and generated text; each generation is cut at 2,048 tokens or a newline

Actions

Text in the prompt: the world model is queried with (state, action) and writes the next state; the policy samples d candidate actions per expansion

Prediction

Sampled next-token decoding at temperature 0.8; one LLM generation per state transition; rewards from action log-probability, answer confidence (majority over several samples) and the probability of 'Yes' to 'Is this reasoning step correct?'

Decoder

None; states are text

Memory

The MCTS tree stores text states and Q-values; reward prompts hide the history and feed only the current state

Speed

No latency figure; all experiments on 4× NVIDIA A5000 24 GB (authors). Per iteration: d expansions × (action proposal + next-state generation + reward queries) plus a roll-out to a terminal state, each a 33B decode [D: structural, from Algorithm 1]

Key detail

RAP(20) with LLaMA-33B solves 42% of 6-step Blocksworld tasks vs 40% for GPT-4 CoT; cost grows with iterations × depth × branching and is bound by memory-bandwidth-limited decoding

Status and sources

EMNLP 2023. Availability: code. Sources: arXiv 2305.14992 Sec. 3.1-3.3 (world model, rewards, MCTS), Sec. 4.1 (LLaMA-33B, T 0.8), Table 1; arXiv 2305.14992 App. A (MCTS changes), App. B.1-B.2 (decoding limit, 4× A5000), Algorithm 1; LLaMA arXiv 2302.13971 Table 2 (33B config, fetched from ar5iv to fill the layer/width/head numbers).

arXiv · code · SVG

TU Dortmund · 2023 · 19M

Transformer-XL over three tokens per step

RL world modelread

Details
Overview

A Dreamer-style agent whose dynamics model is a causal Transformer-XL instead of a GRU. A CNN VAE turns each 64x64 observation into 32x32 categorical latents; latent, action and reward enter as three separate tokens per step, and the hidden state read from the action token drives MLP heads for the next latent, reward and discount. The policy acts from z_t alone, so the transformer runs only in training and imagination, where the XL memory doubles throughput to 39,000 samples/s on one A100.

Representation

32 categorical variables x 32 classes per step from a CNN VAE on 64x64 grayscale frames (stack of 4)

Core

Transformer-XL: 10 layers, d 256, 4 heads of 64, FFN 1024, SiLU; dynamics model 10.8M, world model 19M (Table 5); norm placement not disclosed

Attention

Causal with relative positions; history 16 steps = 47 tokens (3x16-1) [D], plus Transformer-XL segment memory

Actions

Own action token through a modality-specific linear embedding; h_t is read from the action token's output

Prediction

One pass per imagined step; MLP heads give the next latent (categorical sample), reward (mean) and discount

Decoder

CNN decoder trains the VAE only; the policy is conditioned on z_t, so nothing is decoded in imagination

Memory

Cached XL segment outputs: imagination 39,000 samples/s with the memory vs 19,900 with a vanilla transformer (~2x) [D]

Speed

Imagination 39,000 samples/s on one A100 at batch 400 and ~10 h per Atari run (authors); policy 653 frames/s on a CPU

Key detail

3 tokens per step, against 1 in STORM and 17 in IRIS; the transformer is never needed at deployment

Status and sources

ICLR 2023. Availability: code. Sources: arXiv 2303.07109 Sec. 2.1 (tokens, Transformer-XL), Table 4 (hyperparameters), Table 5 (parameters), App. A.1 (wall-clock); verified_findings Finding 3 (STORM Table 1: TWM 3 tokens per step, 10 layers).

arXiv · code · SVG

University of Toronto · 2022 · size not disclosed

Transformer over object slots, one pass per frame

Object-centricread

Details
Overview

The reference object-centric dynamics model. A frozen SAVi (or STEVE) encoder turns each frame into a handful of object slots, and a small transformer encoder over the slots of the last T frames predicts all of the next frame's slots in one pass, then rolls out autoregressively. There are no actions; rollouts feed video prediction, VQA and PHYRE planning. The transformer sees only tens of tokens per step, so the encoder and the per-slot spatial-broadcast decoder carry most of the compute.

Representation

N object slots per frame from a frozen SAVi (STEVE on Physion): 6-8 slots of 128-d (192-d on Physion) at 64×64 or 128×128; a linear layer maps slots to d_e = 128 (OBJ3D) or 256

Core

BERT-style Pre-LN transformer encoder: N_T = 4 layers on OBJ3D and CLEVRER, 8 on Physion and PHYRE; 8 heads; FFN 4×d_e; parameter count not disclosed (~3M block weights for 4 layers at d 256 [D]); activation not disclosed

Attention

Full bidirectional self-attention over the T×N slot tokens of the history; temporal-only sinusoidal positional encoding so slots of one frame share it (permutation equivariant); T = 6 burn-in frames on OBJ3D and CLEVRER (6 × 7 = 42 tokens on CLEVRER [D]), 15 on Physion, 1 on PHYRE

Actions

None; unconditional video prediction, with VQA and PHYRE task-success readouts on the rollouts

Prediction

One pass predicts all N next-frame slots jointly: the last N outputs go through a linear layer plus a residual from the current slots, L2 slot loss (+ image loss); K = 10 rollout frames, predictions fed back

Decoder

Frozen SAVi spatial-broadcast CNN decoder (16×16 broadcast grid) renders each slot as RGB plus alpha mask; STEVE's transformer decoder on Physion

Memory

Sliding history of T frames = T×N tokens; no KV cache (bidirectional encoder)

Speed

No inference figure; 'can be trained on servers with 4 modern GPUs in less than 5 days' (authors)

Key detail

~42 tokens per step through a 4-layer encoder: the attention is negligible, the SAVi encoder and per-slot decoder dominate

Status and sources

ICLR 2023. Availability: code + weights. Sources: arXiv 2210.05861 Sec. 3.2-3.3 (architecture, training), Sec. 4.5 ablations (N_T, T, K, P.E.); arXiv 2210.05861 App. C Table 8 (per-dataset N, D_slot, D_e, N_T, T, K), App. C text (8 heads, FFN 4×, Pre-LN, 16×16 broadcast); Reproducibility statement (4 GPUs, < 5 days); github.com/pairlab/SlotFormer (code and weights).

arXiv · code · SVG

University of Geneva · 2022 · ~30M

GPT over VQ codes, one token at a time

RL world modelverified

Details
Overview

The archetype of the token-level world model for reinforcement learning. A VQ-VAE turns each 64x64 Atari frame into 16 discrete codes, and a small GPT predicts the next frame's codes one token at a time, together with reward and termination. The agent is trained entirely inside this imagination. Each imagined frame costs 17 dependent transformer passes, which is the cost later designs attack.

Representation

16 VQ codes per 64x64 frame, vocabulary 512 (VQGAN autoencoder without the discriminator)

Core

GPT-2-style causal transformer: 10 layers, d 256, 4 heads (minGPT)

Attention

Causal over all tokens; context 20 steps = 340 tokens; KV cache reset at 340 tokens

Actions

One action token between frames

Prediction

Next-token softmax; 17 single-token passes per frame (1 action + 16 codes); reward and termination are read from the action token

Decoder

VQ-VAE CNN decoder; the actor-critic reads decoded frames, so it runs during imagination

Memory

Full causal context, ~3.5 MB of KV per sequence in fp16 [D]

Speed

No inference figure reported; ~3.5 A100-days of training per game (authors)

Key detail

Mean human-normalized score 1.046 on Atari 100k; 17 serial passes per frame

Status and sources

ICLR 2023 (oral, notable top 5%). Availability: code + weights. Sources: arXiv 2209.00588 Tables 3-4, 6; github.com/eloialonso/iris world_model_env.py (17 passes); DIAMOND arXiv 2405.12399 (30M count).

arXiv · code · SVG

Rutgers / KAIST · 2022 · size not disclosed

Dreamer with a transformer in place of the GRU

RL world modelread

Details
Overview

The first transformer world model in the Dreamer setting. The Transformer State-Space Model (TSSM) replaces the RSSM's GRU: the deterministic state h_t is a causal transformer over the past stochastic latents and actions, one token per step, and the posterior drops h_t so every step trains in parallel. Everything else is DreamerV2: CNN encoder and decoder, discrete latents, reward and discount heads, actor-critic in imagination. The transformer is tiny (2 layers), so imagination is latency-bound per step and attention over the growing imagined history is the only cost that scales.

Representation

DreamerV2 CNN encoder; posterior q(z_t | x_t) computed from the frame alone (no h_t), discrete stochastic latent; full state is the concatenation [h_t, z_t]

Core

TSSM: 2-layer transformer, 10 heads, attention and MLP hidden size 200 (DMC) or 600 (Atari), no dropout, no gating, no identity-map reordering (except Atari Pong); ~0.5M (DMC) to ~4.3M (Atari) block weights [D]

Attention

Causal over past steps: h_t = transformer(z_{1:t-1}, a_{1:t-1}); relative positional embedding (Transformer-XL style) is a tunable option; sequence length per DreamerV2 config

Actions

The action is part of each step's input token together with the stochastic latent; how z_t and a_t are combined is not stated

Prediction

Prior p(z_t | h_t) sampled and fed back; 1 transformer pass per imagined step; image, reward and discount predictors read (h_t, z_t); ELBO with KL(q(z_t|x_t) || p(z_t|h_t))

Decoder

DreamerV2 CNN decoder from (h_t, z_t), used for the reconstruction loss and visualisation only

Memory

Attends over the whole (z, a) history of the training sequence or imagined rollout; no KV cache mentioned; transformer memory forces only K = 3 imagined trajectories per replay sample (DMC, Atari)

Speed

No wall-clock or throughput figure; hardware not stated. On DMC and Atari it reaches returns comparable to Dreamer but is 'slower to saturate in general' (authors, Sec. 5.5); on Crafter it imagines until the trajectory's max step (App.)

Key detail

One token per step and a 2-layer core: the template for TWM, STORM and UniZero; the parallel-training trick (posterior without h_t) is what makes the transformer usable here

Status and sources

arXiv preprint (v2 Nov 2024). Availability: closed. Sources: arXiv 2202.09481 Sec. 3.1 and Table 1 (TSSM components), Sec. 3.2 (prioritized replay, K imagined trajectories); arXiv 2202.09481 App. A.3 (2 layers, 10 heads, hidden 200/600, no gating/dropout, K = 3), Fig. 6 (rollout); DreamerV2 config referenced in App. A.3 (github.com/danijar/dreamerv2) for encoder/decoder and latent type.

arXiv · SVG

UC Berkeley · 2021 · size not disclosed

GPT over binned states, actions and rewards

RL world modelread

Details
Overview

Offline RL as one big sequence-modeling problem: every state dimension, action dimension, the reward and the reward-to-go are discretized into 100 bins and become separate tokens of a small GPT. There is no learned encoder and no policy network; acting is beam search over the model's own trajectory predictions, extended one token at a time. Latency scales with state dimensionality, and the authors note it can take seconds per action, which rules out real-time control.

Representation

Each of the N state and M action dimensions, the reward and the reward-to-go is one token: per-dimension uniform or quantile discretization into V = 100 bins; input vocabulary V × (N + M + 2), output logits over V

Core

GPT-style decoder: 4 layers, 4 heads, token embedding d 128, dropout 0.1; parameter count not disclosed (~12·4·128² ≈ 0.8M block weights if the MLP is 4× wide [D])

Attention

Causal over all tokens; context 5 transitions of (s, a, r, R) = 5 × (N + M + 2) tokens, e.g. 125 tokens for a 17-D state and 6-D action [D]

Actions

Action dimensions are ordinary tokens in the stream, decoded after the state tokens of the same step

Prediction

Next-token softmax, one token per pass, teacher-forced training; planning = beam search, width 256, horizon 15 transitions, observations decoded greedily (k_obs 1), actions sampled from the top 20 tokens; offline RL ranks transitions by reward plus reward-to-go instead of log-probability

Decoder

None; states are discretized scalars, decoded back by bin centres

Memory

Fixed context of 5 transitions; no KV-cache details given

Speed

'Up to multiple seconds for action selection when the context window grows too large', hardware not stated (authors, Sec. 6); training 6-12 h per model on one V100 for 80 epochs (authors, App. A)

Key detail

Per executed action: 15 × (N + M + 2) sequential single-token decodes with the 256 beams batched, e.g. 375 for HalfCheetah [D]; a latency-bound sub-1M-parameter workload

Status and sources

NeurIPS 2021. Availability: code + weights. Sources: arXiv 2106.02039 Sec. 3.1 (tokenization, 4 layers/4 heads), Sec. 3.2 (beam search, reward-to-go), Algorithm 1, Sec. 6 (seconds per action); arXiv 2106.02039 App. A (d 128, dropout 0.1, V100 6-12 h), App. E (beam width 256, horizon 15, V 100, context 5, k_obs, k_act); Environment dimensions for the [D] examples: D4RL HalfCheetah (17-D state, 6-D action).

About this gallery

Architecture diagrams for world models whose dynamics model or generative backbone is a transformer, drawn in one visual language after the LLM Architecture Gallery. Numbers marked [D] in the details are our own arithmetic; speeds are the developers' own figures on their own hardware.

Corrections and new models are welcome as issues or pull requests. Cards and diagrams: CC BY 4.0. Fonts: IBM Plex and Saira (OFL).

Changelog

2026-10-21 (version 2)

  • Every card now leads with a bottom-up stack diagram in the style of the LLM Architecture Gallery: small boxes with one label each, repeated blocks with an N × marker, residual skip lines into ⊕, side inputs, zoom-in insets, and all numbers in annotations outside the model.
  • New renderer `wmgallery/stack.py` with a condensed mode for slides; specs live in `MODEL["flow"]` (see `docs/FLOW.md`).
  • The renderer checks every leader line and warns when one crosses a box; all 49 diagrams pass.
  • The earlier token-square card stays available under each diagram as a compact summary.

2026-10-21

  • First release: cards for the models covered by the "Transformer-based world models" research (RL world models, discrete-token video models, causal diffusion transformers, driving and robot models, embedding predictors, world-action models, LLM, object-centric and SSM designs).
  • Renderer: one declarative spec per model produces the web card (SVG) and a compact slide card (PNG).

How to read a diagram

Data flows from the bottom up: input, encoder, the transformer block, the sampling loop, output heads, decoder. Click a card's diagram to open the detailed version; click Details for the facts.

  • one operation
  • attention (the label names the mask)
  • encoder, tokenizer or decoder
  • action or conditioning module
  • repeated block, with its N × marker
  • + residual add
  • zoom-in on one box
  • sampling or rollout loop
  • 12 numbers sit beside the model

Evidence: verified facts passed a 3-vote adversarial check; read facts come from the paper or code; claim facts come from a developer page only.
